rows.section: Observable by a package: owned local editor commands
rows.gnu: GNU supplies the complete command/completion, Dired and file policy libraries.
rows.romacs: The default workspace uses separate Romacs-owned Lisp orchestration: interactive command-name completion/history and a read-only local directory browser with GNU-style long metadata columns, semantic filename faces and n/p/RET/^/g/q. The C-locale ordinary-file listing matches the GNU reference; locale collation, ACL/security indicators and special-device size columns are not implemented. Control-character filenames remain explicitly escaped on one row. Local UTF-8 files and directories share native visits; remote handlers, listing switches, Dired mutation commands and the full GNU coding/mode lifecycle remain unsupported (file coding: VM2-WORKSPACE-CODING). The pristine GNU Lisp tree is unchanged; GNU-only startup does not install these owned modules.
rows.why: A useful slim editor path independent of GNU's full diagnostic/startup dependencies. Maintained GUI command tests and private native-keyboard journeys cover the supported slice, not full GNU API parity.

rows.section: Observable by a package: owned local editor commands
rows.mechanism: `erase-buffer` rejection in a narrowed read-only buffer
rows.gnu: The pinned GNU implementation widens before reporting `buffer-read-only`, changing the accessible region despite rejection.
rows.romacs: The native buffer-level guard runs before widening, preserving text, point, restriction and modification ticks on rejection. Any non-nil `inhibit-read-only` bypasses the buffer-level guard; text-property protection is a separate boundary.
rows.why: Deliberate failure-state preservation for editor-owned read-only views. Live pinned GNU probes distinguish the widening side effect; maintained text/byte-buffer tests assert the safer contract and typed condition/data identity.

rows.section: Observable by a package: scoped GUI command bootstrap
rows.gnu: GNU's dumped image normally supplies all of simple.el.
rows.romacs: When simple.el stops at an unrelated unsupported declaration, the GUI separately evaluates the exact source forms for the line-motion command dependency group. Existing definitions are never replaced; the original partial-file result and each supplemental source line remain reported.
rows.why: Decouples C-a/C-e from generic-function bootstrap without native command stand-ins or edits to GNU Lisp; scoped source-loading and original command-loop tests cover it.

rows.section: Observable by a package: field motion boundary
rows.gnu: GNU accounts for display tables, invisibility and composition, and `current-column` caches its last answer by point and modification count (so a `tab-width` change alone can leave it stale).
rows.romacs: Native Unicode text width, tab stops and caret controls are counted without moving point; display-property overrides are not projected, and non-UTF-8 byte text refuses.
rows.why: Plain-text command-motion slice, not a complete display-table implementation.

rows.section: Observable by a package: field motion boundary
rows.gnu: GNU retains every initialized minibuffer and recognizes active enclosing recursive levels.
rows.romacs: The predicate recognizes native minibuffer-window buffer identities and current activation. Hidden buffers from enclosing recursive levels are not tracked by this predicate.
rows.why: Uses the current native window model rather than buffer-name heuristics.

rows.section: Observable by a package: field motion boundary
rows.gnu: GNU constrains motion using sticky field properties and escape/line/capture arguments.
rows.romacs: Field-free buffers, equal positions and inhibit-field-text-motion implement the native unconstrained branch. A detected field signals `VM2 field-boundary motion is not implemented`, rather than crossing it silently.
rows.why: Bounded command-motion support; `prims/field.rs` tests preserve point, argument errors and explicit refusal.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.mechanism: Save-side path expansion, coding and handlers
rows.gnu: GNU dispatches expansion/directory helpers and supports filename coding.
rows.romacs: Final-operation handlers run for the new primitives; selected expansion helpers refuse with named VM2 errors. Existing read/write leaves now reject only selected handlers, not unrelated tables. Non-UTF-8 filename coding and nonrepresentable byte paths remain refused.
rows.why: Staged expansion and full filename codec are not implemented. `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/filesave/README.md`, `evidence/handler-local/`.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.gnu: GNU may prompt on integer overwrite arguments and implements cross-device copying.
rows.romacs: Collision with integer confirmation and EXDEV explicitly refuse without performing copy/delete. Linux atomic no-replace syscall failures propagate; no racy fallback.
rows.why: Local atomic rename subset. `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/filesave/gnu.json`.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.gnu: An integer OK-IF-ALREADY-EXISTS that meets an existing name asks `yes-or-no-p` (batch reads stdin). PRESERVE-PERMISSIONS copies extended (POSIX or NFSv4) ACLs; an SELinux context only in a libselinux build, which the pin is not. `file-name-all-completions` decodes entries with `file-name-coding-system`.
rows.romacs: An integer proceeds while the name is free and refuses with `VM2 <operation> interactive overwrite confirmation` on a collision, before writing. PRESERVE-PERMISSIONS refuses before creating NEWNAME when the source carries an extended ACL. Listing refuses non-UTF-8 file-name coding and a non-UTF-8 entry that passes the prefix test, and gives `./` and `../` first, then `read_dir` order (both readdir). Handlers dispatch as GNU's; expansion handlers refuse (VM2-SAVE-PATH).
rows.why: No prompt from a leaf; the Hermes and gnosis callers pass nil or t. Oracle test `file_names_links_and_copies_match_gnu` (`crates/romacs-vm/tests/real_ert_load.rs`) compares values, errors and the resulting files with pinned GNU.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.gnu: GNU appends six randomized alphanumeric characters without creating a file.
rows.romacs: Same shape/noncreation; random sequence is not GNU PRNG sequence equality.
rows.why: Names are not reservations. `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/filesave/README.md`.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.gnu: GNU uses symlink interlocks, local PID/boot checks and automatic edit/save lifecycle locking.
rows.romacs: Explicit calls implement symlink interlocks, stale removal and conflict callbacks. Automatic modification/lifecycle locking remains unwired; some nested callback errors propagate instead of redirecting to unlock error handling. Nonregular lock files refuse, link-less filesystem fallback and cross-host boot databases are absent. The boot field is omitted (GNU-supported legacy identity) because `/proc/stat` differs from GNU gnulib boot time on this host; live local PID locks are conservatively retained regardless of the supplied boot field. Reboot/PID-reuse stale detection is therefore unimplemented and may report a false conflict instead of deleting a live owner. Current login environment supplies identity; subsequent changes may affect it.
rows.why: Explicit native locking slice, not full lifecycle parity. `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/filelock-save/REPORT.md`.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.gnu: Pinned GNU Linux returns nil by platform assumption; other platforms may query pathconf.
rows.romacs: Read-only ASCII alternate-name/inode/directory-entry measurement returns actual classification. A unibyte non-ASCII name (ENCODE_FILE's output, which `set-auto-coding` passes on) names the file its UTF-8 bytes spell; other bytes are refused. A directory with no unambiguous ASCII witness defers to its nearest ancestor that has one, as GNU's walk up the tree does (`fileio.c:2710`); a directory or witness that changes under the probe is observed again (at most 8 times) until it is stable; unknown classes, unreadable directories, directories still changing after 8 observations, directories over 4096 entries, and no witness up to the root signal `error` with `VM2 filesystem case sensitivity unknown: REASON`. No probe files are created.
rows.why: Owner explicitly requires actual measurement rather than platform constant. No real case-insensitive mount has been qualified. `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/savejourney/case-detection.md`.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.gnu: GNU performs full codec conversion.
rows.romacs: `encode-coding-string` and `decode-coding-string` support nil/no-conversion, UTF-8 and raw-text coding systems, aliases, EOL conversion, simple BOM handling, NOCOPY and last-coding-system-used. GNU ASCII fast paths are retained. Other conversion codecs, coding hooks, BOM-pair detection and buffer destinations explicitly refuse.
rows.why: This is a bounded string-conversion domain, checked against pinned GNU in `tests/coding_strings.rs`; it does not establish general codec or file-coding parity.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.gnu: GNU supports full filename/ID coding and attribute platform semantics.
rows.romacs: Numeric and named-ID file-attributes and local symlink reads are implemented; unresolved user/group lookups fall back to numeric IDs. Non-UTF-8 symlink targets refuse; stat error and concurrent-change domains are not fully qualified.
rows.why: Scoped native blockers; details in `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/savejourney/native-followup.md`.

rows.section: Observable by a package: save batch (WIP, not accepted)
rows.gnu: GNU formats the complete event/sequence and string-property domain.
rows.romacs: Character/string/vector/list formatting, prefix/ESC folding and symbolic event formatting implemented. Compound events explicitly refuse; rich properties and mixed unibyte formatting remain partial.
rows.why: Needed by real GNU help.el prerequisite, not claimed full parity. `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/savejourney/continue-report.md`.

rows.section: Observable by a package: executable image immutability
rows.mechanism: Object-granularity executable-image rehydration cost; opt-in raw-image freeze
rows.gnu: GNU's writable dumped world permits mutation without copying these roots. Live pinned GNU preserves mixed code/data/plist identity, and byte-compiled literals remain mutable.
rows.romacs: Executable restoration copies every reachable supported Lisp object (cons/string), including code literals, plists, condition properties and captures, with one identity memo. Cold IR remains mapped and undecoded: generated uninterned symbol slots root the private literal objects for later decoding and moving GC. The yank-menu fixture costs exactly **4 private Lisp objects / 195 bytes**; this excludes native metadata allocations. Bare `Vm::new` and raw data-image attachment remain **0 / 0** independently. The mixed fixture preserves `eq` and makes mutation through the variable visible to its function, while another strand remains unchanged. Executable Lisp objects are not frozen. Explicit raw `ImageBuilder` graphs remain immutable and their mutation is refused.
rows.why: The retained raw-image freeze is an explicit embedding boundary, not GNU's writable dump semantics. Per-strand heaps share immutable encoded bytes, never mutable Lisp objects or page-level copy-on-write. Copy-on-write semantics are realized eagerly at executable restoration, at the measured **4 objects / 195 bytes** fixture cost rather than GNU's zero-copy writable-dump access. Eager object rehydration and existing symbol roots preserve cross-root and cold-code aliasing without a new GC root class or image-page writes. This is an allocation-cost divergence, not a mutation/identity divergence. Tests: `tests/code_image.rs`, `code_image::image_alias_tests`; oracle: `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/image-freeze-oracle.json`.

rows.gnu: GNU `font.c:2144-2166` scores candidate size including fixed-size fonts, DPI and average-width mismatch, with factor-of-two rejection; `xfaces.c:5850-5907` validates, stores and invalidates realized faces.
rows.romacs: Exact validation accepts duplicates and returns nil, without changing `face-font-selection-order`. Order is stored in VM display state, published to layout, consumed by resolver ranking, and changed orders invalidate previous face publications and resolver primary/character caches. The `:height` versus other-attribute trade-off is **NOT REPRODUCED**: order is honoured only to the extent current StyleScore expresses it (width/weight/slant; Height has zero distance).
rows.why: Fontconfig catalog discards non-scalable candidates and retains no size/DPI fields (`romacs-font/src/fontconfig_catalog.rs:279`); VM2 snapshot drops width/weight/slant (`romacs-vm/src/display.rs:631-636` in lane base); layout Face cannot carry them (`romacs-layout-input/src/lib.rs:23-28` in lane base); StyleScore has fixed default priority and no size term (`romacs-font/src/style.rs:148-179` in lane base). Observable font selection can therefore differ. Widening this coordinated DISPLAY substrate is deferred by owner decision, not impossible. Live pinned validation witnesses: `crates/romacs-vm/tools/primh/font-selection-specs/internal-set-font-selection-order.json`; cache/ranking assertions: `romacs-font/src/resolver/tests/selection_order_test.rs`. Configured family alternatives are now copied/interned into a traced VM root, published as owned state, and successful setters always invalidate previous face publications and resolver primary/character answers. The scalable resolver still uses its existing FontsetPolicy: consuming the new GNU alternative rows is deferred, not approximated with Rust lowercase (GNU uses case-table uppercase comparison, including final-sigma equivalence and Lisp symbol identity).

rows.mechanism: Alternative-font setters and inherited intern/casing substrate
rows.gnu: GNU family setter copies both list-spine levels, interns strings in the current obarray, stores/returns the converted alist and unconditionally frees realized faces. Registry setter instead calls full current-buffer `downcase`.
rows.romacs: Family setter implements shape/error/copy/storage/invalidation semantics; inherited initial-obarray interning loses symbol-name properties and rejects non-UTF8 names. Registry setter remains absent, rather than introducing default-only lowercase.
rows.why: Live family corpus `font-alternative-specs/internal-set-alternative-font-family-alist.json`: `/0045` and `/0046` VALUE pins (symbol-name properties); `/0047` SIGNAL-VS-VALUE pin (unibyte name). Excluded decimal-bignum probe fails in existing reader before invocation (VM2-READ4); excluded custom-case-table probe requires absent current-case-table/set-case-table substrate. Registry requires GNU casetab.c validation/derived-table regeneration and four buffer case-table roots, plus casefiddle.c special lowercase/string semantics; bounded port stopped before a partial implementation.

rows.mechanism: `sort` default comparison, list identity and callback effects
rows.gnu: Default comparator is native `value<`; stable timsort writes sorted elements back into the original list cons cells and exposes its callback/mutation order.
rows.romacs: Default `value<` compares the runtime's numbers, strings, symbols, lists, vectors, bool-vectors, records, markers and buffers with GNU ordering, mismatch data and depth limits; process and symbol-with-position objects remain unavailable. Explicit comparators and keyword parsing work, with stable small-input natural-run/binary insertion. Inputs of 64 or more use stable insertion sort, with differing callback count/order and complexity; intermediate vector mutation/error effects are not matched.
rows.why: Partial implementation, not complete GNU sort parity. Maintained value-order tests cover default sorts, mixed numeric precision, raw-byte names, circular lists and depth-limit recovery. Live corpus `tools/primh/evidence/sort.json` and the small-sort probes retain the separate sort limitations.

rows.mechanism: `mapconcat` property preservation and absent bool-vector constructor
rows.gnu: Concatenation preserves properties from mapped strings and separators; bool-vectors are valid sequences.
rows.romacs: Inherited native concat drops properties (`mapconcat/0021`, GNU bold versus nil). Bool-vector witness stops at missing make-bool-vector (`/0016`).
rows.why: Shared concatenation/property and representation boundaries; live corpus and exact witnesses in `evidence/leaf-sequences/divergences.json`. Pinned GNU itself aborts when a mapping callback truncates its active list; excluded crashing witness retained in pin-probes.json, not synthesized as a condition.

rows.gnu: C variable controls debugger entry when applicable errors escape.
rows.romacs: Variable value/default/special/dynamic-binding contract is implemented, but the VM does not enter GNU's debugger.
rows.why: C variable port only, not a debugger subsystem. Recorded variable probes accompany internal-make-var-non-special in primh; target assertion LEAF_DEBUG_DEFAULT.

rows.gnu: `(symbol-value 2)` signals `(wrong-type-argument symbolp 2)`.
rows.romacs: Signals `(wrong-type-argument listp 2)`.
rows.why: Existing variable-access condition-data gap exposed by internal-make-var-non-special/0018; retained VALUE class pin, no invented oracle answer.

rows.gnu: `Felt` (fns.c:1853) accepts bool-vectors and rejects records/byte-code objects with `wrong-type-argument sequencep`; `Faref` accepting the latter does not make them arrays for Felt.
rows.romacs: Lists, strings, vectors, bool-vectors and existing char-tables work. The two bool-vector missing pins were removed after live GNU replay. Remaining record/byte-compile construction witnesses retain their existing limitations. These are not fake vectors or successful nil results, and the construction errors are NOT claimed to equal GNU's elt errors.
rows.why: Remaining construction boundaries are recorded in `tools/primh/evidence/elt.json`. Closure rejection itself agrees with GNU when only condition and predicate are inspected.

rows.gnu: Printer serializes the circular input `(1 2 1 2 . #2)` in the corpus control.
rows.romacs: Refuses circular list printing without `print-circle`; actual elt circular access is tested successfully at maximum fixnum.
rows.why: Existing printer gap, 1 PRINTER witness in `tools/primh/evidence/elt.json`; not an elt semantic alternative.

rows.mechanism: `elt` on the separate native syntax-table kind
rows.gnu: `(elt (standard-syntax-table) 97)` returns a syntax descriptor cons, because GNU syntax tables are char-tables.
rows.romacs: Refuses with `(wrong-type-argument sequencep TABLE)` rather than inventing a descriptor. This is NOT GNU-equivalent for that valid input. Ordinary CharTable objects are supported, but VM2's separate regexp-host SyntaxTable is not.
rows.why: Inherited VM2-SY1 representation boundary; explicit refusal witness in elt corpus. Repair requires the out-of-scope syntax/char-table substrate, not an elt approximation.

rows.section: Residual interpreted macro calls — KNOWN, PARKED and UNFIXED
rows.gnu: Interpreted execution recognises residual macro calls on every execution, without caching expansions: expansion counts at definition/first/second call are `(0 1 2)` non-eager and `(1 1 1)` eager. See `src/eval.c:3449-3473`, `433-448`, `2763-2787`; original body/call/argument cons identities remain unchanged; weak-reference probes reclaim expansion-created strings and subsequent executions produce distinct closures.
rows.romacs: `force_lazy` compiles the whole body at first call, permanently freezing unresolved calls including untaken branches: `(0 1 1)` non-eager. Under eager loading, or after a previously skipped branch, GNU returns 42 where Romacs signals `invalid-function`. Observable, KNOWN, PARKED and UNFIXED.
rows.why: Reached-call-thunk prototype preserved on `vm2/lazy-macroexpand`, evidence `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/lazy-macroexpand/` on that branch. Rejected on MEASURED cost, not principle: STANDARD WARM 165/6847 → 123/3768 (42 lost files, 3079 lost forms), 165 regressed prefixes, zero gains, 35 real breakages versus one frozen-model expectation, and earlier real-ERT failure. Apparent mule-util 18/18 gain was an artefact of an earlier subr.el form 284 line 3536 preload failure causing non-eager target loading. No fix claimed.

rows.gnu: GNU readevalloop is also used by eval-buffer and eval-region; byte compilation uses its own top-level environment, not runtime sibling evaluation.
rows.romacs: Source load now shallow-expands and sequentially evaluates resulting progn children, resolving former VM2-RECORD-EAGER. The public eval_source compiler API still compiles each complete read form; eval-buffer, eval-region and .elc input remain unavailable. The loader uses a 128-expansion/native-stack guard.
rows.why: Loader repair is not a claim to implement GNU byte compilation or the missing buffer evaluators. GNU source-load and compiled witnesses deliberately differ; see TOPLEVEL-PROGN.md.

rows.gnu: GNU interpreted push can expand macroexp-let2 and gv-letplace once their definitions exist.
rows.romacs: Ordered bootstrap compiles GNU subr.el push before those two macros exist; mule-util.el form 6 line 168 later signals invalid-function. Reloading only the unchanged real push definition after the prefix makes all 18 mule-util forms load in a separate diagnostic.
rows.why: Same early-compilation ordering class as easy-mmode, not cured by the top-level progn boundary; no native Lisp stand-in added.

rows.gnu: GNU aborts a failed dependency load.
rows.romacs: Independently measured ewoc after failed cl-preloaded and help-mode after failed faces retain those extra failed prefixes solely for attribution. A push-definition/subr reload is another independent diagnostic.
rows.why: None is an accepted bootstrap, STANDARD WARM gain or real-ERT execution; strict adapter retains only VM2-ERT-ORDER. See TOPLEVEL-PROGN.md.

rows.gnu: GNU arrayp and sequencep both return nil on records; read reads their printed spelling.
rows.romacs: Native arrayp now returns nil on records and make-list supports the record boundary probes. Bare VM2 still has no sequencep or read primitive; the unchanged record corpus honestly retains six MISSING results for those two symbols.
rows.why: These existing missing APIs are not represented as passing record parity.

rows.mechanism: MEASUREMENT REGIME: retained failed bindings prefix
rows.gnu: GNU aborts a failed loadup dependency.
rows.romacs: Explicit `--bootstrap ordered` retains only bindings.el failure at form 129, line 1225, `(void-function map-keymap)`, then loads easy-mmode after the macro definitions in its prefix. Other failures remain fatal.
rows.why: Diagnostic progress measurement only, not an accepted bootstrap or STANDARD WARM figure; avoid compiling easy-mmode before bound-and-true-p exists.

rows.gnu: Expands buffer-relative names, dispatches matching file handlers and handles native filename bytes.
rows.romacs: Checks the actual kernel `PATH/./` accessibility (including directory/search permission and symlinks), but inherits the shared fileio expander: lexical `let` of default-directory is invisible, non-nil handler tables, named-user tilde, above-root and non-Unicode names are refused. `setq default-directory` works in this expander.
rows.why: Reuses the existing filesystem subset rather than inventing successful answers for unsupported names/handlers; live pinned matrix and mutation proof are in `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/file-accessible-directory.md`.

rows.gnu: `alloc.c:6075–6098` returns nine rows, including `(intervals SIZE USED FREE)`.
rows.romacs: `garbage-collect` runs the existing moving collector at its traced engine boundary and returns the other eight rows, in GNU order. No `intervals` row is returned.
rows.why: `(assq 'intervals (garbage-collect))` is nil: properties use Rust containers, not an interval pool; inventing interval sizes/counts would be false. Pinned GNU shape is recorded in `crates/romacs-vm/tools/primh/evidence/garbage-collect.json`.

rows.gnu: GNU counts its own typed allocation pools and vectorlike objects.
rows.romacs: Counts describe Romacs storage: cons arena entries/reserve; symbol slots excluding private binding slots and freed slots; string headers and actual string bytes; ordinary vector arena entries and element slots/reserve; float arena entries; both buffer variants. Mixed object-arena reserve is not attributed to strings or floats (their typed free pools are empty). SIZE is the corresponding fixed Romacs storage, excluding variable backing allocations; buffers use the shared object-arena slot size. Non-vector Rust objects are not claimed as GNU pseudovectors.
rows.why: Numeric results and pseudovector population differ; this is heap accounting, not a GNU heap-size emulator. No startup objects are allocated.

rows.gnu: `alloc.c:6044` returns nil without collecting when collection is inhibited.
rows.romacs: Existing nested evaluator/compiler regions inhibit collection with `gc_threshold == usize::MAX`; explicit collection obeys the same inhibition and returns nil.
rows.why: Romacs may inhibit in more regions than GNU because parent Rust compilation state cannot move. No collection or fake statistics are claimed in those regions.

rows.gnu: GNU behavior
rows.romacs: VM2 behavior
rows.why: Status

rows.section: Observable by a package: case-table error routing
rows.mechanism: Malformed non-nil standard-case-table extra slots during implicit scratch or legacy `with-temp-buffer` creation
rows.gnu: Buffer initialization repairs the standard table through `set-standard-case-table`; invalid case-table structure signals `wrong-type-argument case-table-p`.
rows.romacs: Normal `get-buffer-create` preserves the typed condition, but legacy implicit/temporary-buffer creation can erase it into a generic error. No successful substitute table is returned.
rows.why: Existing creation error-routing boundary exposed by new case-table validation; not full casing support.

rows.gnu: `casetab.c:init_casetab_once` constructs four ASCII-only tables, subsequently enriched by GNU Lisp before the dumped oracle starts. The pinned dumped oracle maps character 192 to 224.
rows.romacs: Lazily constructs and independently roots all four ASCII startup tables and the canonical-to-equivalence link. Before the GNU enrichment runs, `(aref (standard-case-table) 192)` is nil, not the dumped oracle's 224.
rows.why: Preserve the actual pre-Lisp initialization contract rather than copying post-load Unicode data; table printer representation remains VM2-CT1.

rows.gnu: `src/data.c:531` accepts GNU closure objects with string bytecode; `#[0 "\\300\\207" [42] 1]` is one.
rows.romacs: `byte-code-function-p` is callable but returns nil for VM2's representable objects; the positive reader witness signals `invalid-read-syntax`. VM2 register-code closures are not GNU bytecode.
rows.why: GNU bytecode object representation, reader and producers are absent; this is a bounded negative-domain implementation, not bytecode execution support.

rows.gnu: `admin/unidata/unidata-gen.el` byte-compiles its runtime functions into eight generated tables (`international/uni-name.el`, `uni-old-name.el`, `uni-comment.el`, `uni-decomposition.el`, `uni-category.el`, `uni-combining.el`, `uni-bidi.el`, `uni-brackets.el`): extra slots 1-3 of each `char-code-property-table` hold byte-code objects.
rows.romacs: Those slots hold the symbols of the same functions in source, `rlisp/romacs-unidata.el`, and each of the eight files first requires that library. `tools/romacs_unidata.py` derives the files from the pinned GNU build's output, replacing only the `#[...]` spans. Every other generated `uni-*.el` file is the pinned build's bytes. Verified on all 1,114,112 code points in pinned GNU (`get-char-code-property` and `char-code-property-description` against stock tables), and on Romacs for 16 properties over U+0000-U+2FFFF.
rows.why: VM2 runs Lisp from source (VM2-EV5, VM2-BYTECODE1); compiled code inside data files cannot be read. **Package-observable:** `(char-table-extra-slot (unicode-property-table-internal 'name) 1)` is the symbol `romacs-unidata-get-name`, not a byte-code object, and the `romacs-unidata-*` functions are fbound.

rows.gnu: Enumerates every native buffer slot in native order.
rows.romacs: Only represented forwarded fields plus ordinary locals, in symbol-slot order; details below.
rows.why: Entire native buffer structure is outside this substrate slice.

rows.gnu: Resets all native mode state and invokes variable watchers.
rows.romacs: Resets represented fields and preserves modeled visit state; absent subsystems and watchers are not simulated, details below.
rows.why: Missing case/abbrev/redisplay/watcher substrates are not supplied by this lane.

rows.gnu: `search.c:2344` replaces buffer matches through `replace_range` and applies current-buffer case/syntax tables when FIXEDCASE is nil.
rows.romacs: String and buffer replacement both infer all-caps/initial casing from the match. A buffer replacement is `romacs--replace-range` (change hooks, undo, markers, match-data adjustment), then `upcase-region` or `upcase-initials-region` over the new text, then point after it. Conversion of initial letters shares VM2-CASE1 pinned titlecase limitations; a casing that expands a character follows VM2-CASE3. VM2 has no intangible text, so point always ends after the replacement.
rows.why: Buffer and string cases are compared with pinned GNU in `tests/replace_match.rs`.

rows.gnu: GNU concat converts unibyte non-ASCII pieces into a multibyte result when required.
rows.romacs: Mixed-encoding replacement explicitly refuses copied unibyte non-ASCII pieces when the result is multibyte.
rows.why: Avoid silently corrupting raw-byte characters or text-property coordinates until conversion is implemented.

rows.gnu: GNU direct-call arity errors name the function as a symbol.
rows.romacs: VM2's shared native arity dispatcher names the subr object; condition kind and argument count agree.
rows.why: Shared dispatch representation remains observable.

rows.gnu: GNU retains allocated unused match registers, including startup search history, and reports nonexistent subexpressions inside that capacity; a buffer replacement's `\N` past that capacity signals invalid replacement text and one inside it inserts nothing.
rows.romacs: VM2 uses its retained match-group vector length, so an unused SUBEXP can signal args-out-of-range earlier and its maximum differs, and a buffer replacement's `\N` past the match's groups signals where GNU's capacity may insert nothing.
rows.why: Match-register allocation history is not modeled; successful groups and explicit nil groups retain their normal semantics.

rows.gnu: GNU behavior
rows.romacs: Romacs behavior

rows.gnu: GNU fileio.c:370 walks cons tails until completion or user quit; a circular outer alist does not terminate by itself.
rows.romacs: `find-file-name-handler` matches acyclic alists, operation metadata, inhibition and match-data preservation, but refuses a detected circular outer alist with `(error "VM2 cyclic file-name-handler-alist is unsupported")`. Native filesystem handler invocation remains separately refused by VM2-FILEIO1/VM2-LOCATE1. Live GNU observations and regression tests are in `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/file-name-handler/`.

rows.gnu: GNU `data.c:510` tests `PVEC_SUBR` (`lisp.h:2216`), including unevalled special-form subrs and native-compiled Lisp (`NATIVE_COMP_FUNCTIONP`, `lisp.h:5494`). Live pinned GNU reports `(subrp (symbol-function 'if))` and `(subrp (symbol-function 'get-upcase-table))` as t; the latter also satisfies `native-comp-function-p` and is defined in `lisp/case-table.el:84`, not C.

rows.gnu: GNU `lread.c:2511` reads the complete Emacs syntax. `#s(` (`src/lread.c:3852`) opens a record; at `)` (`:3770-3780`) a first element `hash-table` makes a table through `hash_table_from_plist` (`:3153`: `test`, `weakness`, `purecopy` and `data` by `plist_get`, first pair wins; data must be a proper list of even length, checked before `make-hash-table`), any other first element a record via `record_from_list` (`:3198`); `#s` not followed by `(`, `#s()` and a dot token inside signal `invalid-read-syntax` with the buffered text (`"#sx"`, `"#s"`, `"."`). A `.` is the dot token only when the next character is a control/space character, NO-BREAK SPACE, one of `"';([#?` `` ` `` `,` or end of input (`:4126-4133`); before anything else, `)` and `]` included, it starts a symbol or number, so `#s(hash-table .)` reads `(#s(hash-table) . 16)` and `(a .)` is a list of `a` and the symbol `.`. A dot token outside a list with an element (list start, vector, record, top level, tail) signals `"."` (`:4140`); a closer in the tail position signals the closer (`:3789,3827`). Also `#N=`/`#N#`, the other `#` dispatch syntaxes, and raw unibyte strings (octet 255 remains unibyte)
rows.romacs: VM2 calls its actual source reader with character-index bounds and offsets. `#s(hash-table ...)` is read exactly as GNU, including its error conditions and data and its ignored keys (`crates/romacs-vm/src/reader.rs` `Reader::record`, `hash.rs` `hash_table_from_plist`; 108-case live-GNU corpus `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/hash-read-syntax/`, `tests/hash_read_syntax.rs`), so the `hashtable-print-readable` syntax is supported when reached (not a complete-subr load claim). Radix `#b`/`#o`/`#x`/`#Nr` syntax now has arbitrary-precision results and GNU-matched condition data (183 live pinned-GNU witnesses in `evidence/radix-reader/`). Records now have a distinct traced/forwarded heap representation and `#s(TYPE ...)` reads a record with GNU's 4095-total-slot limit (`tests/records.rs`). Remaining differences: (1) completed `#N=`/`#N#` aliases are supported; forward/self references and other unsupported dispatch syntaxes signal rather than fabricate objects; (2) a hash table read from SOURCE that is being compiled or loaded (a literal `#s(hash-table ...)` in code, as in `shortdoc-doc.el`) is a self-evaluating constant, as in GNU. `##`, `#:NAME`, `#_NAME` and `#!` read as GNU reads them. The dot rule is GNU's for lists, vectors and `#s(` alike (before vm2/hashread lists and vectors used VM2's general delimiter set, so `(a .?x)` and `(a .#s(hash-table))` read a symbol `.?x`/`.#s` and `(a .)`/`.)` were refused); its two remaining differences are VM2-READ2 (NO-BREAK SPACE after a dot) and VM2-READ5 (`"expected )"`). Raw and mixed 22-bit string input is now supported; non-Unicode symbol names explicitly signal, and other reader fault payloads remain partial
rows.why: **Package-observable staged reader:** circular and other dispatch round trips and source-literal hash tables still need reader substrate work.

rows.gnu: GNU `read_minibuf` (`src/minibuf.c:573`) runs a recursive command loop in ` *Minibuf-N*` shown in the selected minibuffer window; RET, C-j and C-g are bound in `minibuffer-local-map` by `lisp/minibuffer.el:3407-3415` to `exit-minibuffer` (`minibuffer.el:3077`) and `abort-minibuffers` (C, `minibuf.c:472`), whose `minibuffer-quit-recursive-edit` (`minibuffer.el:3104`) signals `minibuffer-quit`. `faces.el:2914` appends `face minibuffer-prompt` to the C value `(read-only t)` of `minibuffer-prompt-properties` (`minibuf.c:2697`). After the loop `add-to-history` (subr.el) records the input (`minibuf.c:1095`). In batch, without `executing-kbd-macro`, it reads stdin (`minibuf.c:653-661`)
rows.romacs: VM2 implements both DEFUNs through `defsubr!` (`src/prims/minibuf.rs`, T2) with GNU's argument checks and order, `string_to_object` and read-string's DEFAULT-VALUE rule in Rust, and the loop in Lisp (`src/prims/minibuf.el`, installed on first use). Supported: PROMPT, INITIAL-CONTENTS string or `(STRING . POSITION)`, KEYMAP, READ, HIST (unbound variable set to nil), DEFAULT-VALUE, INHERIT-INPUT-METHOD (accepted; no input methods exist). Different: (1) **input**: the command loop of VM2-KBD1 reads `unread-command-events` and then the executing keyboard macro while `executing-kbd-macro` is non-nil (GNU's batch prompt regime: `execute-kbd-macro`, `ert-simulate-keys`); otherwise VM2 is batch GNU with an empty stdin and signals `(end-of-file "Error reading from stdin")`, unless an embedder attached a host keyboard (the live GUI does: VM2-HOSTIN1), in which case keys are read from it as interactive GNU does; (2) **bootstrap stand-ins**: until GNU's `minibuffer.el` loads, the Lisp half defines minimal `exit-minibuffer` (no innermost-loop checks), `minibuffer-quit-recursive-edit` and `abort-minibuffers` (single level), and binds RET/C-j/C-g, only where nothing is defined or bound; (3) **prompt face**: VM2 starts from the C value, so the prompt has no `face minibuffer-prompt` until faces.el runs (pins `read-from-minibuffer/1747`, `/1751`, `/1752`); (4) **history**: recorded only if `add-to-history` is fbound, so a bare VM2 never updates `minibuffer-history` (pin `/1778`); HISTPOS and the history commands are absent; (5) a character typed after propertied INITIAL-CONTENTS does not inherit its sticky properties, because VM2's `self-insert-command` does not inherit, so `minibuffer-allow-text-properties` returns them on INITIAL only (pin `/1755`); (6) the prompt's `read-only`/`field` properties are set but VM2 does not enforce read-only text, so DEL can delete into the prompt; (7) no `minibuffer-setup-hook` run unless `run-hooks` is fbound, no `minibuffer-exit-hook`, completion-table rebinding or window-configuration restore; `yes-or-no-p` never uses a dialog box; when a command at the prompt deletes the calling window, VM2 leaves the minibuffer window selected instead of choosing another window (the level and `minibuffer-default` are still restored, test `deleting_the_calling_window_does_not_poison_later_prompts`); (8) recursive prompts follow `enable-recursive-minibuffers` but only the refusal path is evidenced
rows.why: **Package-observable**: (1) without a host keyboard, any prompt outside a keyboard-macro/`unread-command-events` context fails instead of waiting; (3)-(5) through text properties and `minibuffer-history`; (6) by deleting prompt text; (7) by hooks and introspection functions. Corpus: 2492 live-GNU cases (`tools/primh/evidence/read-from-minibuffer.json`, `read-string.json`), 5 pinned VALUE

rows.gnu: GNU's `command_loop_1`, `read_key_sequence` and `read_char` (`src/keyboard.c`) and `Fexecute_kbd_macro` (`src/macros.c:276`) are C. In batch with no unread event and no macro input left, `read_char` waits for the terminal indefinitely. `read_key_sequence` applies `input-decode-map`, `local-function-key-map`/`function-key-map` and `key-translation-map`, echoes keystrokes, runs `help-form` on the help character, and rewrites mouse down/drag events; `recent-keys` records every event shape
rows.romacs: VM2 runs them in Lisp (`rlisp/vm/keyboard.el`, installed with the minibuffer's half on first use) behind Rust entry points (`src/prims/keyboard.rs`), in GNU's order: hooks through `safe_run_hooks`, `command-execute`, `this-command-keys` bookkeeping, macro index and `kbd-macro-termination-hook`, `minibuffer-quit` only caught by the macro. Different: (1) with no unread event, no macro input and no host keyboard, a read signals `(end-of-file "Error reading from stdin")`, thrown out of the innermost recursive edit or minibuffer when there is one, instead of blocking; with SECONDS it returns nil at once and never waits on the host keyboard; (2) no echo, `help-form`, menus or down/drag rewriting; GNU's key translation maps (a pending prefix in any of them keeps the sequence open), unbound upper-case/shift fallback, mouse-area prefix keys, default bindings and remapping are kept, and `input-decode-map` and `local-function-key-map` are global rather than per terminal; (3) `recent-keys` records characters, symbol events and symbol commands only; (4) `input-pending-p` and `discard-input` see only `unread-command-events`; (5) without simple.el and subr.el (a bare VM) minimal `command-execute` and `undefined` stand in; (6) no point adjustment after a command, `delayed-warnings-hook`, PRIMARY selection update, or `defining-kbd-macro` recording
rows.why: **Package-observable** for code that reads past its macro input, relies on key translation or echo, or inspects recorded mouse events. `crates/romacs-vm/tests/kbd_macro.rs`: 35 cases equal to pinned GNU batch and the end-of-input cases

rows.mechanism: Keyboard input read by a prompt in the middle of a command (GUI)
rows.gnu: GNU `read_char` (`src/keyboard.c`) first takes `unread-command-events`, then a keyboard macro, then redisplays (skipped while input is pending, `detect_input_pending`) and blocks in `wait_reading_process_output`; `read_minibuf`'s recursive edit runs inside the suspended command on the native stack, and redisplay may run Lisp (mode-line `:eval`). C-g typed while Lisp runs sets `quit-flag` asynchronously and interrupts it. Deleting the last frame runs `handle-delete-frame`/`save-buffers-kill-emacs`. RET is the function key `return`, translated to 13 by `function-key-map`
rows.romacs: Same order: the command loop's `romacs--read-char` (`rlisp/vm/keyboard.el`, VM2-KBD1) takes `unread-command-events`, then the executing macro, then calls `romacs--read-host-event`, engine control like `eval` (`threaded.rs` `reentrant_load`): the suspended register stack leaves the collector's view and collection is inhibited for the wait, redisplay (`Vm::frame_snapshot`, mode-line `:eval` included) runs in its own engine, the embedder (`Vm::set_host_input`, `host_input.rs`; the GUI's `prompt.rs`) paints and blocks on its input channel; pending input skips the redisplay. Different: (1) two internal names are visible: function `romacs--read-host-event` and variable `romacs--host-input` (t while a host is attached); (2) **no asynchronous quit**: C-g is an ordinary key, seen only when a prompt reads it, so it cannot interrupt running Lisp; (3) closing the frame while a prompt waits signals `quit` (catchable); every later read in that command signals `quit` again without waiting, and the GUI exits when the command returns, with no `delete-frame-functions` or kill-emacs query; (4) the GUI translates the Return keysym to 10 (C-j, `native.rs`), so `last-command-event` for RET at the prompt is 10, not 13 (both exit the prompt); (5) keys read from the host are recorded as VM2-KBD1 records them
rows.why: **Package-observable**: (1) by `fboundp`/`boundp`; (2) by a long-running command (no `quit` arrives); (3) by `delete-frame-functions`/`kill-emacs-hook` not running; (4) by commands at the prompt that inspect `last-command-event`; (5) as VM2-KBD1. Not observable: collection is deferred only for the duration of a wait (no Lisp allocates during it except redisplay's)

rows.gnu: GNU stops before hash, NBSP and vertical tab.
rows.romacs: Vertical tab is now handled exactly; hash and NBSP still remain part of ordinary symbol tokens. Only read-from-string/0163 and /0164 remain VALUE pins.
rows.why: Remaining bounded tokenization difference, not a printer gap.

rows.gnu: GNU reads general signed decimal `N.NNe+INF` as infinity: `2.25e+INF` => `(1.0e+INF . 9)`, `-3.75e+INF` => `(-1.0e+INF . 10)`, both numeric.
rows.romacs: VM2 reads these two tokens as symbols with offsets 9/10, not numbers; `numberp` returns nil for both. Pins `read-from-string/0166`, `/0167`, `/0174` are semantic `VALUE` differences, **not** floating-point printer differences.
rows.why: **Package-observable bounded numeric reader:** its existing special-spelling subset is not GNU's general special-float grammar.

rows.gnu: GNU reads a 257-level parenthesized zero at offset 515.
rows.romacs: VM2 signals `invalid-read-syntax` with `"reader nesting limit exceeded at byte 257"`: the source reader rejects depth >256; 256-level input succeeds at offset 513. Pin `read-from-string/0169` is `SIGNAL-VS-VALUE`; `/0173` is the successful lower-bound probe. Decimal integers past the fixnum range read as bignums, as GNU reads them.
rows.why: **Package-observable resource bound:** no nesting expansion in this slice; fail rather than recurse without bounds.

rows.gnu: Pinned GNU accepts `(+ #x2000000000000000 1)` => `2305843009213693953`, numeric `=`/`<=` of that integer with itself => t, and `(car (read-from-string (prin1-to-string #x2000000000000000)))` => the same integer.
rows.romacs: VM2 reads, prints and structurally compares radix bignums, but arithmetic, numeric comparison and min still reject them through the fixnum/float-only numeric consumers. The printed decimal spelling reads back as the same bignum. `%d` now accepts bignums and floating coercions (VM2-FMT1). Integerp/numberp returning t does not imply those consumers support the new representation.
rows.why: **Package-observable staged numeric consumers:** real arbitrary-precision reader storage, not general bignum arithmetic or serialization parity; reject rather than silently round.

rows.gnu: GNU reading `(a . b c)` signals `(invalid-read-syntax "expected )")`.
rows.romacs: VM2 signals `(invalid-read-syntax "dotted list requires one tail at byte 8")`; the same condition symbol does not imply matching condition data. `read-from-string/0170` is explicitly pinned `DATA`. Other reader errors may likewise expose internal messages/byte positions rather than GNU payloads.
rows.why: **Package-observable staged diagnostic contract:** preserve complete actual fault data in evidence rather than hide payload differences as printer behavior.

rows.gnu: GNU `search.c` retains signed match offsets; after `(set-match-data '(2 -1))`, `(match-string 0 "abcd")` returns `"c"` through substring's negative end normalization.
rows.romacs: VM2 stores offsets as unsigned internally; `match-data t` round-trips `(2 -1)`, but extraction rejects the wrapped end and signals `(args-out-of-range "abcd" 2 -1)`. `set-match-data/0507` is pinned `SIGNAL-VS-VALUE`, not a printer gap.
rows.why: **Package-observable bounded regexp state:** signed match state across every consumer needs separate substrate work; this slice documents safe range rejection rather than claim extraction parity.

rows.mechanism: `call-interactively`, `funcall-interactively`, `interactive-form`: the supported spec subset and what VM2 lacks around them
rows.gnu: GNU `Fcall_interactively` (`callint.c:256-801`) asks `interactive-form` through its symbol (`callint.c:305`), evaluates a non-string spec with `Feval` in the closure's lexical environment (`callint.c:316-319`), records on `command-history` through `add-to-history` (`callint.c:325-330`, `780-783`), handles the prefix characters `+ * - @ ^` (`callint.c:364-405`) and every code letter `a b B c C d D e f F G i k K m M n N p P r R s S U v x X z Z` (`callint.c:449-762`), formatting each prompt with `format-message` (`callint.c:457`). `Finteractive_form` (`data.c:1139-1210`) reads the `interactive-form` property along the alias chain, a subr's DEFUN intspec, `CLOSURE_INTERACTIVE`, autoloads (via `autoload-do-load`) and `(lambda ...)` lists. `funcall-interactively` (`callint.c:239-254`) is `Ffuncall` in a frame that `called-interactively-p` (subr.el) finds by walking the backtrace.
rows.romacs: Recorded live against GNU 32.0.50 through primh (`tools/primh/callint-specs/*.json`, `evidence/{call-interactively,funcall-interactively,interactive-form,prefix-numeric-value}.json`, inputs in `tools/primh/logs/callint/make_spec.py`). **Supported and matching GNU row-for-row:** prefix characters `* - ^ @` (`^` calls `handle-shift-selection` when it is fbound; `@` with a window event signals unsupported), `+` error, codes `d e i m p P r R U Z`(no prefix) `N`(with prefix), the reading codes `D f F G` (`read-file-name` through its symbol with callint.c's arguments) and `s` (the `read-string` subr, not its symbol), their prompts through `format-message` (`tests/callint_reading.rs`), invalid-letter error text, `this-command`/`this-original-command`/`real-this-command`/`last-command` save and restore, `current-prefix-arg` (never `prefix-arg`), KEYS vector and `inhibit-mouse-event-check`, RECORD-FLAG history items including `interactive-args`, `history-length` (variable and property), the list-spec path in the closure's own lexical environment, the `interactive-form` property chain, and the GNU intspecs of the VM2 subrs that GNU defines as commands. **Divergent:** (1) the other minibuffer/keyboard-reading codes (`a b B c C k K M n S v x X z`, `N` without and `Z` with a prefix) signals `(error "call-interactively: the input-reading code `X' is not supported in VM2 yet")` where GNU reads input (`call-interactively/0466`, `/0471` pinned `CONDITION`; GNU batch gives `end-of-file`); (2) a `%` in a prompt signals the same kind of unsupported error where GNU formats it (`/0497`, GNU `Not enough arguments for format string`); (3) VM2 has no mark, so `m`, `r` and an active-region `R` always take GNU's no-mark error, and `set-mark` is void (`/0475`); (4) `buffer-read-only`, `inhibit-read-only` are ordinary global specials, not GNU's per-buffer slot, and buffer edits do not enforce them — only `*` reads them; (5) `add-to-history` (subr.el) is void in a bare VM2, so the KEEP-ALL body is run natively, and a non-nil `history-delete-duplicates` signals unsupported; `(interactive SPEC . rows.mechanism: Lisp evaluation depth accounting and native stack exhaustion
rows.gnu: GNU eval.c:2604-2609,3196-3201 checks the dynamically bound integer limit (default 1600, floor 100 on overflow), signals `(excessive-lisp-nesting DEPTH)`, and restores depth on unwind; bytecode.c:783-788 signals plain `error` at compiled call overflow. loadup.el:106 raises the limit to 4200 and :156 doubles it. eval.c:255-277 restores borrowed reserve from CURRENT limit/reserve values; signal_or_quit borrows 20 (eval.c:1969). Per level at limit 100, measured at the pin: interpreted code reaches 30 `eval`-reentry and 45 call levels, byte-compiled 48 and 96. GNU has no recoverable native-stack condition (a C stack overflow is caught and Emacs returns to top level, `keyboard.c:166-169,13426` "Re-entering top level after C stack overflow")
rows.romacs: VM2 consults the forwarded limit at every Lisp activation and shares one budget across eval/load/macro engines; register storage grows and rebases; `eval`/load/lazy-compile/autoload reentry runs on heap stack segments grown on demand (`stacker`), so reentry depth is bounded by the Lisp counter, not by the thread stack. Separately (R193), every activation and every compiler `expr` step refuses when fewer than 256 KiB of native stack remain, with a recoverable `(error "native stack exhausted during Lisp evaluation")` or `... while compiling Lisp` (compiler recursion is refused, not grown). Accounting is GNU bytecode's: 50 and 99 levels at limit 100 (`tests/eval_depth.rs` `reentry_and_call_levels_follow_gnu_bytecode_accounting`). Measured sustainable depth (exactly 4200 and 8400 reached, then `excessive-lisp-nesting`): on the GUI evaluator's explicit 64 MiB stack for plain calls, `apply` and `run-hooks` recursion and `eval` reentry in debug, gate (optimized, no LTO) and release (LTO) builds; on a 2 MiB thread in debug and release for every shape. `signal-hook-function` borrows twenty levels from `lisp-eval-depth-reserve` (default 200), restoring on normal/error/throw exits
rows.why: **Package-observable:** (1) VM2 always signals `excessive-lisp-nesting`, also where GNU bytecode signals plain `error`; recursion reaches more levels than GNU's interpreter (50 vs 30, 99 vs 45). (2) GNU's debugger reserve borrower is not implemented. Returning `handler-bind` callbacks borrow 200 levels and restore the current limit/reserve after normal or nonlocal exit. (3) In the gap between the native guard and the Lisp limit -- reached only on small threads in optimized non-LTO builds (2 MiB: `apply` recursion refused before depth 4200, `run-hooks` before 8400; 8 MiB: 8400 reached) or with a raised limit (50000 levels on 2 MiB) -- code sees a plain `error` with that message instead of `excessive-lisp-nesting`, and a handler for `excessive-lisp-nesting` alone does not catch it; it is never a process abort. GNU's 4200/8400 loadup raises are effective at the GUI's 64 MiB. See `src/eval_depth.rs` and `tests/eval_depth.rs`.

GNU `kill-buffer` runs query functions, aborts on nil, runs the kill hook, detaches the buffer and repairs windows. Modification state compares SAVE_MODIFF with MODIFF, not text; real undo may explicitly restore clean via saved-modtime undo metadata
rows.romacs: While GNU files.el is unavailable the GUI uses explicitly named romacs adapters over native primitives. `romacs-gui-visit-file` uses native exact-name, saved-truename and revalidated device/inode identity, reusing hardlinks, symlinks, equivalent paths and direct Lisp native visits without losing edits. Failed GUI visits are cleared/killed rather than adopted as successful empty buffers. Startup consumes `+LINE[:COLUMN]` and `--`. Save is a no-op when native `buffer-modified-p` is nil; otherwise native stat-only `verify-visited-file-modtime` checks nanosecond time and recorded size, without disk-content reads. Conflicts install future-key y/n/C-g overwrite confirmation: y writes and refreshes metadata; n/C-g preserve both versions. Same modtime/size content changes are deliberately not interrogated, matching GNU. Removed files also prompt here, unlike GNU recreation policy. A dynamic mode-line `*`/`-` reflects native modification counters, including inverse edits to saved bytes. Existing GNU mode-line-format is preserved. C-x k now truly kills the captured buffer after y (clean buffers immediately), runs native query/hook lifecycle and honors vetoes; dead identities remain buffer objects, leave registries, detach markers/overlays and are replaced in windows. C-x C-c/native close confirm modified GUI visits, including hidden visits. Non-answer/prefix input or buffer switch cancels pending consent instead of GNU modal reprompting; GUI confirmation is an asynchronous adapter, not GNU userlock.el. Native kill lacks process/indirect/autosave/lock/update-hook lifecycle and GNU window-history policy (see crates/romacs-vm/GNU-DIVERGENCES.md). Native alias lookup is named `romacs-find-buffer-visiting`, not full GNU `find-buffer-visiting` predicate/handler support; noncurrent anonymous visits are not enumerated. No native undo record/replay, backups, save hooks or GNU interactive write echo. GNU display-column customization/ctl-arrow/C1 controls are not fully implemented for startup positions
rows.why: **User-observable and package-observable**: ordinary supersession, confirmed/vetoed kill, hardlink reuse and counter-based modified indication are implemented. Packages can call native get-file-buffer, modified-state and kill primitives, but do not acquire GNU save-buffer/find-file/userlock/undo Lisp through these adapters. Exact timestamp, callback-list mutation, omitted kill subsystems and alias lookup limits remain observable. A reverse edit remains modified; a real GNU undo-to-save may become clean and cannot yet run in VM2. Interactive GNU write messages and FIFO no-reader/deadline behavior remain deliberate divergences described in VM2-FILEIO1.

rows.mechanism: zero-length strings and vectors are not unique objects
rows.gnu: Every zero-length string is one of two shared objects and every zero-length vector is `zero_vector` (`src/alloc.c:2329-2330,2358-2359,2903,3424`): `(eq "" "")`, `(eq (copy-sequence "") "")`, `(eq (vector) [])` and `(eq (substring "abc" 3) "")` are all t, and `(substring "" nil nil)` returns its argument.
rows.romacs: VM2 allocates a fresh object for each empty string or vector, so all of those are nil. Pinned in the bulk `core` corpus as `eq/0476`, `eq/1067`, `substring/1585`, `substring/1669`, and found independently by primh's `alias` family as `substring/8251`, `substring/8263` (`tools/primh/evidence/substring.json`; all class `VALUE`).
rows.why: **Package-observable identity:** code that tests `(eq s "")` instead of `(string-empty-p s)`/`(equal s "")` takes the other branch. Contents, length, `equal` and printing are identical. Canonicalising empties is an allocator change (a rooted shared object per kind), deliberately not folded into the primitive batch that found it.

rows.mechanism: `format` never returns its format string itself
rows.gnu: When formatting produces no change, `styled_format` returns the FORMAT argument itself (`src/editfns.c:4301-4304` at pin `45b0f7699df`, `if (! new_result) { val = args[0]; ...}`): `(let ((s (copy-sequence "abc"))) (list (eq (format "%s" s) s) (eq (format s) s) (eq (format "%s" "") "")))` is `(t t t)` on GNU 32.0.50.
rows.romacs: VM2's `format` always allocates a fresh string: the same form is `(nil nil nil)` (measured, `romacs-vm --eval-stream`, lane `vm2/bulk1`). `string-trim` and `string-replace` share GNU's no-change identity but are void in VM2 today, so they are not yet a divergence.
rows.why: **Package-observable identity only:** code that tests `(eq (format ...) s)` to detect "nothing changed", or that mutates the result expecting to leave the argument intact (GNU would mutate the argument), behaves differently. Contents and properties match. Not fixed in the `core` batch, which does not touch `format`; recorded because it was known and unrecorded.

rows.mechanism: a closure is not a sequence in VM2
rows.gnu: A closure is a vector-like object in GNU 32.0.50, so `length`, `append` and `mapcar` accept it as a sequence: `(length (lambda (x) x))` is 5 for the byte-compiled closure and 3 for the interpreted one (both regimes recorded; `src/fns.c:154` at pin `45b0f7699df`, `Flength` counts a `CLOSUREP` object's slots).
rows.romacs: Ordinary VM2 closures remain opaque objects: all three signal `wrong-type-argument`. Explicit `make-interpreted-closure` values and marked OClosures expose their supported metadata slots; this does not make ordinary closures sequences. Pinned in the bulk `core` corpus as `length/0071`, `append/1041`, `mapcar/0257` (class `VALUE`; the probes catch the type error as -99 so the closure is never printed).
rows.why: **Package-observable, rarely:** only code that measures or walks a function object's slots (OClosure internals, some debuggers/`cl-print`) sees the difference. General closure sequence operations remain out of scope. OClosure uses the explicit metadata boundary described in VM2-OCLOSURE1.

rows.mechanism: calling a symbol whose cell is a macro: `invalid-function` without data
rows.gnu: `funcall`/`apply` of a symbol whose function cell is a macro signals `(invalid-function SYMBOL)` (`src/eval.c` `funcall_general`): `(progn (fset 'q '(macro . car)) (condition-case e (funcall 'q 1) (error e)))` and the same through `(assoc 2 '((1 . a)) 'q)` both give `(invalid-function q)` on GNU 32.0.50.
rows.romacs: VM2 refuses the call with the text fault "invalid function: macro is not callable" (`crates/romacs-vm/src/threaded.rs` `invoke_full`, `t2_resolve`), so the condition is `invalid-function` with NO data: `(invalid-function)`. Funcalling the literal `(macro . car)` matches GNU. Pre-existing (present at `0aded923`); found by the second Sol review of `vm2/bulk1`, not changed by it.
rows.why: **Package-observable data only:** handlers that dispatch on `invalid-function` still catch it; code reading `(cadr e)` to name the offending function sees nothing.

rows.mechanism: `mapcar` is a Lisp function in VM2
rows.gnu: `mapcar` is the C subr `Fmapcar` (`src/fns.c:3551`, arity `(2 . 2)`): `(subrp (symbol-function 'mapcar))` is t, and a wrong argument count signals `(wrong-number-of-arguments #<subr mapcar> N)`.
rows.romacs: VM2 defines `mapcar` in its built-in prelude (`crates/romacs-vm/src/prims/prelude.el`) because a Rust primitive must not call Lisp from a loop (GC doctrine): `subrp` of it is nil, `symbol-function` returns a closure, and a wrong count signals the compiled-closure form `(wrong-number-of-arguments (2 . 2) N)`. Its traversal, element order, length-first checking, shortening by the callback and its signals match GNU case for case on the bulk `core` corpus, except the four arity rows `mapcar/0203`-`0206` (pinned `DATA`) and a closure used as the SEQUENCE (`mapcar/0257`, VM2-CLOSEQ1).
rows.why: **Package-observable metadata:** code inspecting `subrp`/`subr-arity` of `mapcar`, or reading the function datum of its arity error, sees a closure. Ordinary calls over lists, vectors, strings and bool-vectors are indistinguishable.

rows.mechanism: `defcustom` stores the raw default form where GNU stores a thunk, and `:set` is never invoked
rows.gnu: Measured on GNU 32.0.50 for `(defcustom e-opt (progn (setq n (1+ n)) 7) "d" :type 'integer)`: `(get 'e-opt 'standard-value)` is `((funcall #'#[nil ((progn (setq n (1+ n)) 7)) (t)]))` — a list whose car is a **form that calls a closure** wrapping the default — so `(eval (car (get 'e-opt 'standard-value)) t)` returns `7` and re-runs the side effect. A `:set` function runs **once at definition**. `custom-variable-p` answers non-nil
rows.romacs: VM2 stores the **raw unevaluated form**: `standard-value` is `((progn (setq n (1+ n)) 7))`. `(eval (car (get 'e-opt 'standard-value)) t)` **signals `void or non-function`** rather than returning 7, and the side effect does not re-run. A `:set` function is recorded under `custom-set` but **never invoked** — the setter counter stays 0 where GNU's reaches 1. `custom-type` and the other keyword properties match GNU, and **`custom-variable-p` matches GNU exactly** (`t` for a `defcustom`-defined symbol, `nil` otherwise). No theme machinery (removed by R90)
rows.why: **Package-observable** in two ways. Code that recomputes a default via `(eval (car (get 'sym 'standard-value)) t)` — which is what Custom itself does — gets an error instead of the value. Code relying on `:set` running at definition time silently does not get its setter called, so a variable whose setter has side effects beyond `set-default` is left uninitialised. Ordinary reads of the variable's value are identical, and `custom-variable-p` is not a difference. Revertible: wrap the stored form so `eval` of the car yields the default, and invoke `custom-set` at definition

rows.mechanism: A local `(defvar x)` reaches `let` but not lambda parameters
rows.gnu: GNU's `funcall_lambda` (`src/eval.c:3433`) binds arguments by consing onto `lexenv` whenever `lexenv` is non-nil and **never** consults a local-special marker, while `Flet`/`FletX` (`eval.c:1109`, `:1183`) check `declared_special` and `Fmemq (var, Vinternal_interpreter_environment)`. A one-argument `Fdefvar` enters the interpreter environment only
rows.romacs: VM2 matches GNU: the compiler's parameter-binding path does not consult local specials, while its `let` path does. Verified on live GNU 32.0.50 interpreted with `lexical-binding: t` on line 1 — the lambda-parameter form signals `void-variable`, the `let` form answers 18
rows.why: **Not a divergence in behaviour**; recorded because VM2 briefly implemented the symmetric (wrong) rule and a reader may expect symmetry. Both directions are pinned by `local_declaration_does_not_reach_lambda_parameters_but_does_reach_let` and mutation-proven

rows.mechanism: A globally special name binds lambda parameters dynamically
rows.gnu: GNU's `funcall_lambda` (`src/eval.c:3433-3436`) binds every parameter of a lexical closure by consing onto `lexenv` whenever `lexenv` is non-nil, without consulting `declared_special`; the byte compiler also binds such a parameter lexically. Live GNU 32.0.50 over `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/file-local-special/flr.el` (`(defvar flp-x 0)`, then `(funcall (lambda (flp-x) (flp-get)) 42)` where `flp-get` reads the dynamic value): `(0 43)` interpreted and `(0 43)` byte-compiled (`gnu-cache-kinds.txt`)
rows.romacs: VM2's compiler binds a parameter dynamically when its name is globally special (`declare_special`/`defvar` with a value), so the same fixture answers `(42 43)` (`vm2-af1209d0-probes.txt`): the callee sees the argument instead of the global value. `let` matches GNU (dynamic)
rows.why: **Package-observable** for code that names a lambda or `defun` parameter after a global special variable (the byte compiler warns about it) and relies on callees NOT seeing the argument; found while reviewing VM2-FILESPECIAL1's cache key, which now records global and file-local declarations separately because they compile differently. Revertible by binding parameters lexically regardless of global specialness in the compiler's parameter path

rows.mechanism: A file-local `(defvar x)` reaches the rest of its file only when it is a bare top-level form
rows.gnu: `Fdefvar` with one argument (`src/eval.c:990-996`) conses SYMBOL onto `internal-interpreter-environment` when that is non-nil; `readevalloop` (`src/lread.c`) binds the variable once for the whole file and evaluates each form with `eval_sub`, which does not rebind it, so the declaration makes SYMBOL dynamically bound by every LATER `let` and closure of that file and of no other file. A `progn`, `when` or binding-less `let` around it does not rebind the environment either, so `(progn (defvar x))`, `(when t (defvar x))` and `(let () (defvar x))` at top level all persist; `(when nil (defvar x))` does not run and declares nothing. Live GNU 32.0.50: `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/file-local-special/` (`gnu-transcript.txt`, `nested-forms.txt`)
rows.romacs: VM2's loader records a top-level form that is exactly `(defvar SYMBOL)` once it has evaluated, and seeds the root compilation of every later form of the same file with those names (`crates/romacs-vm/src/loader.rs`), saving and restoring the set around each `load`; the source cache keys its validity on them, so an identical form in a file without the declaration is recompiled. A declaration nested inside a top-level `progn`/`when`/`let` still reaches only the rest of its own form (the compiler's existing local-special scope, VM2-VD1), so GNU's `(1 2 3 unbound)` for the four nested shapes above is VM2's `(unbound unbound unbound unbound)` past the form. `eval-buffer`/`eval-region` are not covered. Before this row (fixed on `vm2/defvar-local`) even the bare form reached nothing past itself, which made cl-macs.el's `(defvar cl--loop-args)` (line 939) ineffective. The source caches (in memory and persistent) key a cached form on each name's declaration KIND, lexical / file-local / global (`Vm::special_kind`), and the persistent cache's portable compiler reproduces file-local declarations as file-local (Sol review of af1209d0: it had made them global, so a warm load bound a lambda parameter dynamically where the cold load bound it lexically; `tests/file_local_special.rs`). Also different, pre-existing and not introduced by this row's fix (measured by that review, `evidence/file-local-special/fld.el`, `gnu-cache-kinds.txt`): `(defvar nil)` and `(defvar t)` signal `cannot declare a constant` where GNU returns `nil` and `t`; `(special-variable-p 'nil)` and `(special-variable-p 't)` are nil where GNU answers t; and a one-argument `(defvar x)` executed inside a function that is called at top level declares nothing for later forms, where GNU's later `let` binds x dynamically (fixture: GNU `(t t 9 7)`, VM2 `(nil nil 9 unbound)`)
rows.why: **Package-observable** for files that declare a variable special inside a wrapping top-level form and bind it in later forms; the bare `(defvar x)` that cl-macs.el and most of `lisp/` use behaves as GNU

rows.mechanism: VM2 keymap skeleton is installed lazily
rows.gnu: GNU builds `global-map`, `esc-map`, `ctl-x-map`, `function-key-map`, `key-translation-map` and `special-event-map` while loading `lisp/subr.el` and `lisp/bindings.el`, so by the time any user Lisp runs these variables are already bound to keymaps (`src/keymap.c:syms_of_keymap` defines the variables; the maps themselves come from Lisp)
rows.romacs: VM2 boots without loading `subr.el` and installs the same skeleton on **first use of any keymap primitive** rather than in `Vm::new`. Reading `global-map` (or the other five) before calling any keymap primitive signals `void-variable`, where GNU returns a keymap; after any keymap primitive runs, the variables are bound and behave as GNU
rows.why: **Package-observable** only by Lisp that reads one of these six variables without first calling a keymap function, which `bindings.el` and ordinary configuration do not do. Chosen so a freshly constructed VM allocates nothing: the collector's tests assert exact heap contents and arena indices, and a constructor-time skeleton silently redefines "empty heap" for all of them. Revertible by calling `initialize_keymaps` from `Vm::new` and converting those GC tests to arena-relative indices

rows.gnu: `keyboard.c:command_loop_1/read_key_sequence` accumulate prefixes, translate events, invoke hooks and call `call-interactively` (`callint.c:Fcall_interactively`) on the binding
rows.romacs: G2a translates native Unicode/control/named events, consults existing keymaps and runs the bound command through the real `call-interactively` primitive (VM2-CALLINT1 lists its spec subset). No prefix accumulation, command hooks, prefix-arg transfer or macro-specific undefined signalling. `this-command-keys` is a single-event vector. `interactive` evaluated as a form returns nil
rows.why: **Package-observable staged subset**. Any closure with an `(interactive ...)` form, whether made by `defun`, `defalias`, `fset` or an anonymous `lambda`, is a command. [Exact contract/evidence](crates/romacs-vm/COMMAND-LOOP.md)

rows.mechanism: GUI command-loop errors in the echo area
rows.gnu: `keyboard.c` `command-error-default-function` prints the error with `print_error_message` into the echo area and rings the bell; `command_loop_1` clears the echo area when the next command starts. `call-interactively` of a key bound to a symbol with no function signals `(wrong-type-argument commandp SYMBOL)` (GNU 32.0.50: `Wrong type argument: commandp, romacs-nonexistent-cmd`)

A command that returns normally leaves its last message (`message`, or printing to `t`) in the echo area, without its text properties. Data that cannot be re-read (`#<buffer x>`) falls back to `CONDITION: DATA`. VM2's `call-interactively` of a void command signals `(wrong-type-argument)` with no data, so `M-x` under `--gnu-lisp` shows `Wrong type argument` where GNU shows `Wrong type argument: commandp, execute-extended-command`. rows.why: **User-observable** echo text; the void-command signal data is Lisp-visible through `condition-case` (a VM2 divergence, surfaced here, not introduced)

rows.gnu: `keyboard.c:make_lispy_event` and live GNU 32.0.50 `(kbd "C-SPC")` yield `[67108896]`, while C-@ is zero

rows.gnu: `src/xdisp.c:display_mode_element` (`:28458`) and `decode_mode_spec` (`:29429`): buffer-local formats per window, propertized strings with their own text properties, conditionals, field widths/precision, risk filtering, every percent escape over the C state (coding systems, frame name, recursion depth, processes, save point); `src/window.c:Fwindow_vscroll/Fset_window_vscroll` support character units, numeric scroll values and preserve-vscroll
rows.romacs: Tier B evaluates each window's format with that window's buffer current, its window point installed as buffer point (`redisplay_window`, `xdisp.c:20620-20641`), and the window temporarily selected (`display_mode_lines`, `xdisp.c:28114-28156`); the real selection is rooted across collecting `:eval` forms, and buffer point and selection are restored after evaluation, including error/throw/quit, before choosing the active/inactive face (same-buffer split oracle `crates/romacs-vm-gui/evidence/tierb/gnu/point-context.txt`): buffer-local formats, `:eval`/`:propertize` (face symbol or first face of a face list), conditionals, integer field widths and precisions, risky-variable filtering, `*too-deep*`/`*invalid*`, and `%b %f %* %+ %& %l %c %C %p %P %o %q %i %I %n %m %M %@ %- %%` exactly as GNU 32.0.50 formats them (oracle `crates/romacs-vm-gui/evidence/tierb/gnu/mode-line.txt`). Without the C state GNU reads: `%z` is `-` and `%Z` is `-` plus `eol-mnemonic-undecided` (GNU: the buffer's coding mnemonic, `UUU:` for utf-8-unix); `%F` is `Emacs` (GNU tty `F1`, GUI frame title); `%[ %]` are empty (no recursive edit); `%s` is `no process`; `%e` is empty, which is GNU's answer on a `SYSTEM_MALLOC` build such as glibc GNU/Linux even while `memory-full` is non-nil (`xdisp.c` `decode_mode_spec` `case 'e'`; oracle `crates/romacs-vm-gui/evidence/tierb/gnu/standard-head.txt`), where a gmalloc build shows `!MEM FULL! `; `save_modiff` stays 0 (no `set-buffer-modified-p`/save), so any edit shows `**` until the buffer dies; text-property changes (`put-text-property`, `remove-text-properties`) do not count as modifications, where GNU's `modify_text_properties` (textprop.c) bumps MODIFF when a property actually changes, so a buffer changed only in its properties shows `--` here and `**` in GNU; `mode-name` has no buffer.c default `"Fundamental"`. Assigned `%m`/`%f` values and `%Z`'s explicit EOL mnemonic accept both multibyte and unibyte strings; unibyte high bytes are projected to octal glyph text before field-width/precision handling (not GNU's raw-byte character counting). A string's own text properties and anonymous face plists are not projected onto the band. GNU stops producing band glyphs at the window's last visible column (`xdisp.c:30105`); VM2 builds band text up to four times the frame's columns and the painter clips it at the window edge, so the visible band is the same, and both keep evaluating `:eval` elements past the edge. Field widths and integer limits wrap to a C `int` as GNU's do (`xdisp.c:28663`, `:28879`; 32.0.50 transcript `crates/romacs-vm-gui/evidence/tierb/gnu/field-wrap.txt`: a limit of 2305843009213693951 is -1, a one-column precision, so the next element stays visible), then VM2 clamps them to 2^20 columns; the clamp only changes text beyond the band's four frame widths, which neither side shows. A format string's literal run is selected by columns (TAB `tab-width`, other control characters 2, GNU `c_string_width`) and then counts its characters toward precision and padding, as `store_mode_line_string` does; `%`-spec results and literal strings truncate and pad by characters (`crates/romacs-vm-gui/evidence/tierb/gnu/control-width.txt`). A control character that fits is painted `^X`; GNU's painted form of a TAB in a mode line has not been compared. Band faces follow GNU's `CURRENT_MODE_LINE_ACTIVE_FACE_ID`: the selected window draws `mode-line-active`, others `mode-line-inactive` while `mode-line-in-non-selected-windows` is non-nil; because faces.el (which defines `mode-line-active` inheriting `mode-line`) is not loaded, an undefined `mode-line-active`/`mode-line-inactive` falls back to `mode-line`. Vscroll requires explicit pixelwise non-nil and a nonnegative u32 integer; other units, floats, negative clamp and fourth setter argument are rejected
rows.why: **Package-observable**: `%z`/`%Z`/`%F`/`%m` text, the modified flag after a save, and band faces from string properties differ; `format-mode-line` itself is not implemented. Escapes, constructs and per-window evaluation follow GNU within the restrictions above

rows.mechanism: VM2 logical-line reveal policy and owned GUI defaults
rows.gnu: `src/xdisp.c:redisplay_window` (`:20470`): honours a forced start once and moves point to the middle row when point is not displayed (`:20742-20901`); otherwise `try_scrolling` when `scroll-conservatively`, `scroll-step` or `scroll-margin` ask for it, else recentre via `move_it_vertically_backward` over wrapped screen lines (`:21230`)

Positive integer `scroll-conservatively` values choose minimum scrolling within that many lines; values above 100 always reveal minimally. The owned GUI defaults this Lisp policy to 101, so ordinary navigation does not jump to the centre; zero retains automatic centering. Refused GUI vertical movement at the first/last accessible line preserves point. `scroll-step`, `scroll-margin`, `scroll-preserve-screen-position`, `make-cursor-line-fully-visible` and `auto-window-vscroll` remain ignored; a partially visible last row cannot hold point
rows.why: **Observable by a package** that sets the scroll variables or relies on continuation lines; with GNU's defaults and lines narrower than the window, `window-start` after redisplay matches GNU
