rows.gnu: `src/syntax.c` `forw_comment`, `back_comment`, `Fforward_comment`, `scan_lists`, `scan_sexps_forward` read each character's syntax through gl_state, whose interval bookkeeping can lag the scan position in rare backward-then-forward property cases; `parse_sexp_propertize` and `find_defun_start` call Lisp mid-scan
rows.romacs: `crates/romacs-vm/src/syntax_scan.rs` transcribes the scans with every comment style, nesting, fence, escape and prefix flag, and looks syntax up at the exact position (GNU's intent). Where GNU calls `internal--syntax-propertize` or `syntax-ppss`, the T2 primitive stops, performs the call, and reruns the deterministic scan from the first run's start, coerced positions, initial parse state and variables, replaying the syntax the stopped run read, so calls, arguments, order, results, GNU's three error checks and the find_start cache match. The scan's variables (`parse-sexp-ignore-comments`, `comment-end-can-be-escaped`, `open-paren-in-column-0-is-defun-start`, `comment-use-syntax-ppss`, `parse-sexp-lookup-properties`) are read when it starts; GNU reads all but `multibyte-syntax-as-symbol` live, so a `syntax-propertize` function that changes one mid-scan affects later positions there and none here. Each run reads the buffer's flat text, so a scan after an edit first flattens the buffer, and N propertize calls cost N scan prefixes. A signal muted in `internal--syntax-propertize` is logged with GNU's `Error muted by safe_call` text through `message` under `inhibit-message`, which VM2 does not yet record in `*Messages*`
rows.why: **Semantics match pinned GNU on `tests/syntax_scan.rs` (55 cases, two find_defun_start regimes) and 99/100 GNU `test/src/syntax-tests.el` bodies under the full loadup bootstrap when its resource file is inserted directly (Romacs `find-file` cannot yet read it; the 100th needs `byte-compile`).** Cost is linear in buffer size per call, not gap-buffer local.

rows.mechanism: regexp search that GNU answers with "Stack overflow in regexp matcher" only after >1,066,664 failure-point pops
rows.gnu: freezes (minutes: `a*a*a*b` over 100,000 `a`s), then the overflow error if the limit is ever reached
rows.romacs: GNU's backtracker decides such a candidate under a 1,066,664-pop budget; past it, returns the linear matcher's answer (match or `nil`); overflows GNU reaches on its first descent are unchanged
rows.why: R92/R93: "experienced by the end user as 'Emacs froze'"; reproducing that error means reproducing the freeze

rows.gnu: `buffer.c:Fkill_buffer` calls `reset_buffer_local_variables(b, 1)` to clear all locals, including permanent ones; `data.c:Fkill_local_variable` removes one entry and restores the default; `buffer.c:Fkill_all_local_variables` normally preserves non-nil `permanent-local` bindings and filters `permanent-local-hook` lists
rows.romacs: VM2 locals follow live buffer keys in private key-weak tables. Collection drops dead-owner entries, compacts their private table storage, and recycles inactive private binding slots; live owners and active dynamic bindings retain and forward their values. `kill-buffer` now eagerly removes all symbol-local bindings and forwarded buffer-local state, including permanent locals, and detaches markers and overlays. `kill-local-variable` and `kill-all-local-variables` remain missing. Both the native fallback and completed GNU `with-temp-buffer` kill an externally retained temporary buffer on unwind
rows.why: Explicit collectable-buffer subset, not full GNU buffer killing or major-mode reset; private `#:vm2-buffer-local-values` tables/slot IDs are implementation details, not supported Lisp interfaces

rows.mechanism: Ordinary mode/startup calls are data-model operations only
rows.gnu: `buffer.c:Fforce_mode_line_update` returns ALL and marks live redisplay; GNU Lisp modes also initialize syntax, keymaps, hooks and frame menu state
rows.romacs: VM2 `switch-to-buffer` selects/creates the current named buffer but ignores NORECORD/FORCE-SAME-WINDOW; nil buffer selection is rejected. `emacs-lisp-mode` sets buffer-local `major-mode` only. `menu-bar-mode` changes its boolean variable only; `menu-bar-lines` is a standalone 0 default and does not track a frame or mode. `force-mode-line-update` returns ALL without scheduling display work. `truncate-lines` is nil by default and local when set

rows.gnu: `print.c:738-915`, `print_object` support all GNU objects, controls and graphs.
rows.romacs: VM2 now honors list/vector length, list level, quote/function shorthand, newline/control/multibyte escapes, supported overrides and shared/cyclic cons/vector/nonempty-string numbering with `print-circle`. NaN payloads are preserved by these entry points. Without `print-circle`, cyclic lists and vectors still refuse instead of GNU's `#0` ancestor notation; depth over 100 refuses. Hash-table print-length refuses; circular/shared hash-table traversal is not modeled. Backquote/comma shorthand and full GNU symbol-number recognition remain incomplete. Obarrays, text-property strings and fresh/uniform character tables are represented, including property-value cycles with `print-circle`; sparse/historical table layout remains VM2-CT1. Unsupported structural layouts still refuse, including marker objects themselves (distinct from supported marker stream destinations); ordinary compiled closures print opaquely as `#<interpreted-function>`, without exposing source, capture cells or array slots. The owned cl-print method delegates to this native printer. Existing frame/terminal diagnostic representations remain VM2-FRAME-PRINT.
rows.why: Partial serialization contract, not full GNU printing parity. Existing circular-printer pins in other corpora remain distinct from the new `tools/primh/printing-specs` finite live-GNU matrix.

rows.gnu: GNU `print.c:print_prepare`, `Fterpri` and `printchar` accept buffer/marker streams, preserve point, run modification hooks and output objects incrementally.
rows.romacs: Romacs emits to buffer streams, markers in multibyte buffers, rooted T2 callback functions/symbols and batch stdout. `t` is the echo area, as on GNU's terminal, only where `noninteractive` is nil and the embedder declares it renders one (`Vm::set_echo_area_host`: the live GUI); a print there extends the message printing made, and any other message starts a new one (`message_buf_print`). Every other host, `noninteractive` or not, prints `t` toBuffer/marker output follows GNU point motion and restores the current buffer on errors; unibyte-buffer markers explicitly refuse. Output that runs no Lisp is inserted natively and recorded in `buffer-undo-list`; when change hooks or `undo-auto--undoable-change` can run it goes through `insert`'s bracket (`romacs--print-insert`), as print_finish's insert_1_both and signal_after_change do, including the after-change of empty output. `terpri` with non-nil ENSURE refuses, including non-function streams (only the function refusal matches GNU). Rendering is snapshotted before callbacks, so callback mutation of remaining graph/print controls is not reflected. Quoted non-ASCII unibyte strings to callback/stdout streams refuse; `princ` raw strings retain their actual character codes. `write-char` matches GNU uint32 callback conversion, but unsupported stdout character codes refuse.
rows.why: Buffer/marker comparisons are in `tests/printing_streams.rs` and `tests/print_change_hooks.rs`; ENSURE and incremental callback mutation parity remain outside the supported boundary.

rows.mechanism: Full printer controls and override errors
rows.gnu: GNU `print.c:658-736` and `print_object` implement every print variable and exact malformed-override conditions.
rows.romacs: The supported controls are read dynamically; print-circle numbers objects in GNU's preprocessing order and keeps print.c's Lisp-visible `print-number-table` (with print-continuous-numbering carrying it and the label index across calls; sub-char-tables are not entered in it); non-nil float-output-format, print-integers-as-characters, print-unreadable-function, print-charset-text-property and print-symbols-bare explicitly refuse before traversal, even when a given object would not use that option. Malformed/unknown override errors currently differ from GNU. `princ` plain-string fast path does not consult these controls.
rows.why: Explicit conservative refusals, not silent ignored settings. Each measured exception is pinned in the new printing corpus.

rows.gnu: GNU `charset.c:838-1215` validates and publishes OFFSET, MAP and parent definitions; MAP calls `load_charset(..., 0)` after publication even with `inhibit-load-charset-map`.
rows.romacs: OFFSET, MAP initial metadata, SUBSET and SUPERSET definitions are implemented, including dense code indices, fastmaps, partial identity publication on missing maps, and ISO/Mule ordering. `decode-char`, `encode-char` and `map-charset-chars` use per-record encoder/decoder tables built from the `:map` or `:unify-map` entries as `load_charset` does, and `unify-charset` marks OFFSET charsets unified (de-unifying a unified charset is refused). MAP search honors relative default-directory paths; tilde expansion and non-ENOENT file-error payloads are not yet equivalent to GNU openp.
rows.why: `Vchar_unify_table` itself is not a Lisp-visible object here, and `inhibit-load-charset-map`'s dump-time temp tables are not modelled. Code-space array access covers vectors, records, strings and ordinary char-tables. Native syntax-table layouts, bool-vectors, and interpreted/compiled closure arrays remain outside this bounded domain and can signal arrayp where GNU reads an element.

rows.gnu: `chartab.c:676` compares sub-table entries with `equal` (nil), `eq`, or by calling TEST for each pair.
rows.romacs: nil, `equal` and `eq` collapse sub-tables exactly as GNU does (printed structure compared with pinned GNU); any other TEST signals `(error "VM2 optimize-char-table supports only the equal and eq tests")`.
rows.why: Calling Lisp per comparison would need a T2 continuation through the recursive walk; GNU's preloaded Lisp uses only the default test.

rows.gnu: `composite.c:692` replaces the gstring cache and returns `(clear-face-cache t)`, nil.
rows.romacs: Returns nil. VM2 composes no characters and keeps no gstring or display face cache to clear.
rows.why: Lisp sees GNU's value; character composition itself is absent (`composition-function-table` is a plain char-table nothing reads).

rows.gnu: `DEFVAR_PER_BUFFER` with the `fraction` predicate (`buffer.c:5678,5691`): setting a value other than nil or a float in [0.0, 1.0] signals `wrong-type-argument`.
rows.romacs: Both are per-buffer and auto-local with GNU's nil default; any value is accepted.
rows.why: No VM2 redisplay reads them yet; cus-start.el only needs them bound.

rows.mechanism: Change hooks and undo for buffer text primitives
rows.gnu: `insdel.c` runs `before-change-functions`, `after-change-functions` and `first-change-hook` around each change and records it in `buffer-undo-list` (`undo.c`).
rows.romacs: Insertion (`insert`, `insert-and-inherit`, `insert-before-markers`, `insert-before-markers-and-inherit`, and through them `insert-char` in GNU's 4000-byte pieces, `indent-to`, `move-to-column` with FORCE and `insert-buffer-substring`), deletion (`delete-region`, `delete-and-extract-region`, `erase-buffer`, `delete-char`), `self-insert-command` (cmds.c's amalgamation, abbrev expansion, auto-fill and `post-self-insert-hook`), `subst-char-in-region` and the text-property setters share one bracket after insdel.c: buffer and text read-only refusals (an insertion's by stickiness), `undo-auto--undoable-change`, the characters' `modification-hooks`, `insert-behind-hooks` and `insert-in-front-hooks`, the overlays' hooks, file locking, `select-active-regions`, `first-change-hook`, and `before-change-functions` and `after-change-functions` with GNU's arguments, with `inhibit-modification-hooks` bound, a failing hook variable reset and `deactivate-mark` set. They record GNU's undo entries (merged insertions, deletions with marker adjustments, point and first-change entries, `record_change`), and each command first runs `undo-auto--add-boundary` and notes point as command_loop_1 does, so GNU's `undo` restores typed, deleted and killed text. No Lisp runs when no hook can run and undo is off or undo-auto is absent. Remaining: `combine-after-change-calls` deferral, and `overwrite-mode` self-insertion before the end of the buffer, refuse before anything changes; `translate-region-internal` runs no change hooks and records no undo; `insert-file-contents` runs fileio.c's bracket for a read that is not a visit (prepare_to_modify_buffer at point, signal_after_change over the inserted text) but records no undo; undo lists are never truncated (no truncate_undo_list at collection); a unibyte buffer's change bounds and deletion start are not carried through the before hooks (it holds no markers); a deletion whose start the before hooks moved outside the accessible region signals `args-out-of-range` before anything changes, as GNU does when it records undo or returns the text, where GNU without undo deletes outside the restriction; hooks run by `subst-char-in-region` with NOUNDO see the buffer's own undo list and file name, which GNU binds off; `self-insert-command` rings no bell without `ding`. `replace-match` in buffers, `transpose-regions` and the region case commands do not exist yet.
rows.why: The bracket is native and calls its Lisp half (`rlisp/vm/insdel.el`) only when a hook can run; the remaining primitives join it as they are ported (their replace_range semantics first).

rows.gnu: A GNU build with libxml2 returns t and provides `libxml-parse-html-region` and `libxml-parse-xml-region` (`xml.c:321`).
rows.romacs: VM2 links no libxml2: `libxml-available-p` returns nil, as a GNU built without HAVE_LIBXML2 does, and the two parsers are void.
rows.why: Callers test the predicate and fall back to xml.el (dbus.el, url-dav) or to text rendering; `shr`/`eww` HTML rendering needs a parser and is not available yet.

rows.gnu: A GNU build with tree-sitter returns t once the library loads and provides the `treesit-*` parser primitives (`treesit.c:5295`).
rows.romacs: VM2 has no tree-sitter: `treesit-available-p` returns nil, as a GNU built without HAVE_TREE_SITTER does, and the parser primitives are void.
rows.why: `*-ts-mode` major modes are unavailable; packages that check the predicate (treesit.el's own defcustoms, sh-script, org-src) take their regexp font-lock paths.

rows.gnu: `editfns.c:2509` translates unibyte buffers byte by byte and may put raw-byte characters (a unibyte table's non-ASCII bytes, BYTE8) into a multibyte buffer
rows.romacs: VM2 translates multibyte buffers as GNU does (in-place one-for-one rewrites keep properties; other replacements follow `replace_range`'s point and marker rules); a unibyte buffer, or a result that is not a Unicode character, signals an explicit VM2 error before that replacement
rows.why: A VM2 multibyte buffer holds Unicode text; ucs-normalize and other callers map characters to characters

rows.gnu: `fns.c:4334` inserts each decoded octet above 127 into a multibyte buffer as a raw-byte character
rows.romacs: VM2 decodes into unibyte buffers, and into multibyte buffers when every decoded octet is ASCII, as GNU does; other octets for a multibyte buffer signal an explicit VM2 error before the buffer changes
rows.why: A VM2 multibyte buffer holds Unicode text (VM2-TRANSLATE1, VM2-FILEIO1); decoding binary data is done in a unibyte buffer, as svg.el and image callers do

rows.mechanism: `replace-region-contents` past MAX-SECS with a vector SOURCE
rows.gnu: `editfns.c:2155` falls back to replacing the region with SBUF's whole accessible text, not the SBEG..SEND the vector names
rows.romacs: VM2 falls back to SBEG..SEND; everything else (GNU's comparison and edit script, markers, point, undo, hooks, MODIFF, and INHERIT reaching replace_range as its adjust-match-data flag) follows the pinned source and is compared with it
rows.why: The fallback only runs when the comparison times out or lacks memory, and replacing with text the caller did not name would corrupt the region

rows.gnu: process.c and callproc.c: process objects (`make-process`, `make-pipe-process`, `make-network-process` for every socket kind, `make-serial-process`), filters and sentinels run by `wait_reading_process_output` in every wait (`accept-process-output`, `sleep-for`, `sit-for`, and the command loop's idle wait), which also runs ordinary and idle timers (keyboard.c `timer_check`); SIGCHLD wakes the wait; `call-process` reads its output incrementally, with DISPLAY redisplaying
rows.romacs: Process objects, `make-process` (pipes or a pty), `make-pipe-process`, `call-process`, `call-process-region`, signals, filters, sentinels and the wait are GNU's transcribed (`crates/romacs-vm/src/subprocess.rs`, `prims/process.rs`, `rlisp/vm/subprocess.el`). Limits, each an explicit refusal or a stated difference: `make-network-process` makes TCP stream servers and clients only, refusing datagrams, local sockets, `:local`/`:remote` addresses, numeric families, non-numeric service names, `:tls-parameters` and `:use-external-socket`; a `:nowait` client connects without blocking and the wait reports its outcome (the `open` sentinel or `failed`, after trying each further address) as GNU does; `make-serial-process`, `process-attributes`, `list-system-processes`, `set-process-thread` and the datagram functions are void. Waits never read the keyboard and run no idle timers (`timer-idle-list`), and the GUI host's command loop neither runs timers nor reads process output: both happen only inside Lisp waits. `call-process` reads all output before inserting it, so DISPLAY never redisplays; a quit does not kill its child. Exited children are found by a polled `waitpid` and pidfds, not SIGCHLD; children a dropped VM leaves are reaped by the host's one shared reaper thread where GNU's exit leaves them to init. Process output is decoded per VM2-PROC2
rows.why: **Package-observable:** asynchronous network code beyond TCP, serial ports and idle timers cannot run, so `current-idle-time` is always nil (keyboard.c:4949 answers nil whenever Emacs is not idle); GUI sessions see process output and timers only while Lisp waits

rows.gnu: detect_coding chooses the decoding of output read with an `undecided` coding system from the bytes and `coding-system-priority-list`, possibly a non-UTF-8 system
rows.romacs: VM2 detects ASCII and UTF-8 only (`prim/leaf/process.rs` `decode_output`): ASCII output keeps the undecided coding system, UTF-8 output is decoded as the matching `utf-8` EOL variant, and other bytes signal `error` rather than being guessed
rows.why: **Package-observable:** a process whose output is neither ASCII nor UTF-8 and has no explicit coding system fails with an error; one that names its coding system is unaffected

rows.gnu: frame.el and faces.el dispatch on the frame type to `x-`, `w32-`, `ns-`, `pgtk-`, `haiku-`, `android-` and `tty-` C primitives; a batch session answers for its initial terminal, approximating colors to 8 tty colors (`tty-colors.el`)
rows.romacs: rlisp/romacs-frame.el answers every one of them from one capability record, `romacs-display`. Without a GUI the record is pinned GNU's batch answers (not graphic, 0 color cells, 3 planes, `mono`, `dark`, the 8 standard colors), so package tests see GNU's batch values; colors keep tty-colors.el's names and approximation over the record's palette. No `tty-*` terminal primitives exist; the GUI does not set the record yet, so GUI frames still answer as batch does (VM2-WIN5)
rows.why: **Package-observable** in the GUI until it sets the record: graphic-only features stay off. Frame geometry, edges, z-order and mouse-position queries are not yet owned

rows.gnu: `fns.c:internal_equal` includes structural marker/overlay, record, bool-vector and char-table rules
rows.romacs: Deep cons/vector/string/float comparison, cyclic graphs, string properties ignored; other runtime objects use identity. Two separate markers at the same position compare nil (measured in s124-vm-probes.json)
rows.why: VM2 has no record/bool-vector/general char-table representation; marker/overlay/closure equality remains staged

rows.gnu: GNU load/library search considers compiled/native/compressed suffixes and load policy
rows.romacs: Searches load-path (or explicit PATH), .el then the literal name; honors NOSUFFIX. INTERACTIVE-CALL is accepted without UI/message effects. No .elc/.eln/compressed resolution
rows.why: VM2 loads source; lookup does not pretend to find an executable compiled library

rows.mechanism: VM2 is not an Emacs daemon
rows.gnu: `emacs.c:Fdaemonp/Fdaemon_initialized` inspect daemon state and reject initialization in a non-daemon
rows.romacs: `(daemonp)` is nil; `(daemon-initialized)` errors that this function requires daemon mode (both measured). No daemon state is fabricated
rows.why: Matches GNU non-daemon behavior; daemon startup is not implemented

rows.mechanism: Temporary buffers remain unnamed, collectable internal allocations
rows.gnu: GNU `with-temp-buffer` creates a named buffer then kills it on unwind
rows.romacs: VM2 lowers `with-temp-buffer` to private `#:vm2-temp-buffer`, restores current buffer on unwind, and lets GC reclaim unretained temporary buffers. `generate-new-buffer` is supplied only by GNU's loaded `subr.el`, which composes the native `generate-new-buffer-name` and `get-buffer-create`; a bare VM does not define it. Ordinary named-buffer operations accept ASCII unibyte names as the same names as text strings; non-ASCII unibyte names signal an explicit unsupported error
rows.why: Preserves existing 100,000-temporary-buffer GC regression without retaining every temporary as a named live buffer; no kill-buffer protocol is claimed

rows.mechanism: `set-window-buffer` starts a reassigned window at position 1
rows.gnu: GNU restores the buffer's remembered `b->last_window_start` (`src/window.c:4376-4378`, `set_marker_restricted (w->start, make_fixnum (b->last_window_start), buffer)`), so redisplaying a buffer a window showed before resumes near its former top
rows.romacs: VM2 keeps no per-buffer last window start, so `window-start` becomes 1 and the window scrolls to the top. `window-point` does follow GNU and takes the buffer's own point.
rows.why: Yes — a package reading `window-start` after `set-window-buffer`, or relying on a restored scroll position, sees the difference; revertible by recording a per-buffer last window start

rows.gnu: `current-window-configuration` saves FRAME's whole window tree, the selected frame, focus redirection, minibuffer scroll and selected windows; `set-window-configuration` (`src/window.c:7661`) restores them, consulting `window-restore-killed-buffer-windows` for windows whose buffer was killed and deleting dedicated ones
rows.romacs: VM2 saves and restores the one frame's tree (root subtree and minibuffer window) with each window's buffer, start and point markers, sizes, margins, vscroll, combination limit and persistent parameters, reviving deleted windows as GNU does; current-buffer point, `record-window-buffer` calls and buffer-history cleanup follow GNU. DONT-SET-FRAME has no effect (one frame); no focus frame or minibuffer scroll window is saved; a window whose saved buffer was killed keeps its buffer or gets `*scratch*`, and `window-restore-killed-buffer-windows` is not consulted (VM2 has no dedicated windows to delete)
rows.why: **Package-observable** only for multi-frame code, minibuffer scrolling and custom `window-restore-killed-buffer-windows` functions

rows.gnu: GNU keeps `w->total_lines`/`total_cols` as independent slots: `window_resize_apply_total` (`src/window.c:4905`, DEFUN `:5003`) installs each window's `new_total` without touching pixel sizes, so `(set-window-new-total (frame-root-window) 7)` then `(window-resize-apply-total)` makes `window-total-height` 7
rows.romacs: VM2 derives a window's total size from its pixel size and the canonical character (`window-total-height`), so `window-resize-apply-total` validates FRAME and returns t without changing anything; totals follow `window-resize-apply`. Pin `window-resize-apply-total/0010` (VALUE)
rows.why: **Package-observable** only by a caller that applies totals that disagree with the pixel sizes it applied; GNU's own `window.el` always calls `window-resize-apply` first with matching pixel sizes

rows.gnu: GNU resizes the subtree of an internal WINDOW that takes ROOT's place through Lisp `window--resize-root-window` and `window-resize-apply` (`src/window.c:3467`)
rows.romacs: VM2 scales WINDOW's children proportionally with its frame-resize plan, in Rust
rows.why: **Package-observable** only through the exact pixel split of the surviving children, which can differ by rounding from GNU's resize

rows.gnu: GNU `window_wants_mode_line` (`src/window.c:6037`) reads WINDOW's buffer's `mode-line-format`, whose C default is `"%-"` (`src/buffer.c`), and `window_wants_header_line` likewise reads `header-line-format`; a header line is one line tall
rows.romacs: VM2 answers from what its display draws: a mode line one canonical line tall from `mode-line-format`'s current value cell (as `display.rs` `build_mode_line` reads it), honouring the window's `mode-line-format` parameter and `none`; no header line, tab line, scroll bars or dividers (all 0). A bare VM2 has no default `mode-line-format`, so its windows want no mode line until `bindings.el` sets one. Pins `window-mode-line-height/0006`, `/0011`, `window-header-line-height/0010` (VALUE)
rows.why: **Package-observable**: body sizes computed from these heights match what VM2 draws, not what GNU would draw, in a bare VM and with a header line

rows.mechanism: `delete-other-windows-internal` scroll preservation for a live WINDOW
rows.gnu: Pinned GNU `src/window.c:3484-3488` promises to try to keep previously visible text at its old frame position; `:3533-3538` saves start/top, `:3683-3715` adjusts the start with `vmotion (startpos, startbyte, -top, w)` (`:3701`) and clears vscroll. `src/indent.c:1977-2101` implements vmotion using compute_motion, i.e. visual rather than just newline motion
rows.romacs: VM2 expands the surviving window's geometry but leaves its start unchanged. With 100 `line\n` lines and a lower window starting at 201, expansion leaves 201 instead of pinned GNU's 146. Executable characterization: `tests/window_prims.rs::vm2_win4_expanding_a_scrolled_lower_window_keeps_its_start`; corpus pin `delete-other-windows-internal/0020` (VALUE)
rows.why: **User/package-observable:** C-x 1 / delete-other-windows on a scrolled lower window moves the formerly displayed text to the top instead of attempting to preserve its frame position. This live-leaf path is not covered by any full-parity claim; the differential corpus records a documented mismatch

rows.mechanism: Hybrid frame device type and character metrics
rows.gnu: Pinned GNU `src/frame.c:327-338` delegates live-frame type to framep (`:287-321`): t denotes an initial/termcap frame. Terminal frame-char-height and frame-char-width are always 1 (`:4358-4372`, `:4376-4391`), unlike graphical font metrics
rows.romacs: VM2's one live frame returns t but character dimensions are backend font pixels, initially height 20 and width 10; set_frame_geometry updates them (e.g. 24 and 8), and `frame-native-width` and `frame-native-height` (GNU's `frame-pixel-width` and `frame-pixel-height`) report the frame in those pixels, where a GNU terminal frame reports columns and lines. The batch ERT runner (`romacs-gnu-ert`) sets GNU batch's terminal geometry, 80 columns by 25 lines of 1x1 characters, so package and GNU suites see GNU's frame and window sizes. This is NOT GNU terminal consistency. Joint characterization: `tests/window_prims.rs::vm2_win5_frame_type_and_character_metrics_are_a_documented_hybrid`; pin `frame-live-p/0014` (VALUE) measures all three together
rows.why: **Package-observable:** code taking t to mean character-only terminal units receives non-unit pixel/character conversions. Relative geometry probes alone cannot establish device-model parity; the joint probe records an explicit mismatch

rows.mechanism: Single initial frame and terminal scope
rows.gnu: GNU has traced frame/window/terminal objects (`src/frame.h:145`, `src/window.h:100`, `src/termhooks.h:475`) and supports multiple devices and frame lifecycles
rows.romacs: VM2 now lazily allocates traced Frame/Terminal identities; Frame owns the root, selected and minibuffer windows, and every Window points back to its Frame. Its single INITIAL terminal is not a TTY. Frame creation/deletion, device switching and saved recursive-minibuffer selection are not implemented. `window-list`, `get-buffer-window`, `window-combination-limit`, `terminal-list`, `tty-top-frame` and `last-nonminibuffer-frame` are callable over this actual graph
rows.why: Single-frame subset only; no claim of multi-device parity. Geometry remains the existing pixel backend (VM2-WIN5)

rows.gnu: GNU `minibuffer-selected-window` (`src/window.c:7153`) returns the live saved selection only during an active, selected minibuffer; `src/minibuf.c:827` updates it on real recursive entry
rows.romacs: Unregistered: direct calls and funcall signal `(void-function minibuffer-selected-window)` rather than inventing nil from a depth counter
rows.why: Package-observable refusal, not matching GNU's successful result. The overlay has a lexical calling-window but no native recursive-entry/unwind selection ownership

rows.gnu: GNU `set-window-hscroll` (`src/window.c:1313`) stores clipped columns and affects redisplay
rows.romacs: Unregistered: direct calls and funcall signal `(void-function set-window-hscroll)`
rows.why: Package-observable refusal rather than an inert setter; existing snapshots/layout do not carry horizontal scroll state

rows.gnu: GNU `recenter` (`src/window.c:7219`) uses visual motion, window start, vscroll and redisplay
rows.romacs: Unregistered: direct calls and funcall signal `(void-function recenter)`
rows.why: Package-observable refusal, not a successful no-op or newline approximation

rows.gnu: GNU `frame-visible-p`, `make-frame-visible`, `make-frame-invisible`, `iconify-frame`, `raise-frame` and `lower-frame` (`src/frame.c:3505-3700`) track and change a frame's visibility through its terminal; a batch terminal frame always reads visible and ignores the requests
rows.romacs: VM2's one frame always reads visible, `visible-frame-list` lists it, the requests change nothing, and making the sole frame invisible without FORCE signals GNU's error. `tests/frame_visibility.rs` matches pinned GNU batch
rows.why: **Package-observable** only in the GUI, where iconifying or hiding the window is not performed

rows.gnu: GNU `redisplay` (`src/dispnew.c:7020`) processes pending events and redraws before returning t (nil while a keyboard macro runs)

rows.gnu: GNU `window_text_pixel_size` (`src/xdisp.c:11742`) runs the display iterator (`move_it_to`, `src/xdisp.c:10928`) over the window's buffer: on batch's initial terminal frame in columns and lines (`src/term.c` `produce_glyphs`), on a GUI frame with its fonts and images
rows.romacs: Until a host lays the frame out, which batch never does, VM2 runs a port of that iterator for a terminal frame (`src/prim/leaf/display_motion.rs`, `display_elements.rs`): `char-width-table` widths, tabs, control and escape sequences, display tables, `nobreak-char-display`, `glyphless-char-display`, invisibility and ellipses, `display` strings, spaces (`:width`, `:align-to`, `:relative-width`), margin and fringe specs, overlay strings and their `window` property, line and wrap prefixes, truncation, continuation and `word-wrap`, with GNU's FROM, TO, X-LIMIT, Y-LIMIT, MODE-LINES and IGNORE-LINE-AT-END, in units of the frame's character size. VM2 draws no tab or header line, so MODE-LINES adds only the mode line (VM2-WIN3). It signals `VM2 window-text-pixel-size ... is unsupported` for a `(when FORM ...)` display spec with a FORM other than t or nil (the primitive cannot evaluate Lisp), `(min-width ...)`, physical width units, the `composition` property, `selective-display`, `display-line-numbers`, a horizontally scrolled window, `word-wrap-by-category`, an image line prefix, a unibyte buffer, a unibyte string with non-ASCII bytes under `unibyte-display-via-language-environment`, and strings from two overlays that share a start: GNU orders those by when its overlay tree last inserted each (`move-overlay`, or insertion before a front-advance start, reinserts), which VM2 does not record. Automatic compositions are not applied (VM2-WIDTH1). After a host has applied a layout, the same motion runs over the host's layout (`src/prim/leaf/display_hosted.rs`): within the call the VM hands the attached `LayoutHost` the window's buffer text and the faces its snapshot paints, and the host answers each character's advance and row height from the code that paints it (`romacs-layout2` `LayoutEngine::measure`), presenting nothing. The last visible x is the text area less the continuation or truncation glyph's advance, as on a GUI frame without fringes. MODE-LINES adds the host's band: the last painted band's height, else the mode-line face's (GNU's CURRENT_MODE_LINE_HEIGHT). rows.mechanism: Variable watchers run with collection inhibited
rows.gnu: `add-variable-watcher` (`src/data.c:1857`) accepts any function; `notify_variable_watchers` calls it before every `set`, `let`, `unlet`, `makunbound` and `defvaralias` of the variable, with WHERE the buffer of a buffer-local binding
rows.romacs: VM2 keeps GNU's `watchers` property and `get-variable-watchers`/`remove-variable-watcher`, and calls every watcher before `set`, `set-default` and `defvar` (as `set`), `let`, `unlet`, `makunbound`, `kill-local-variable` and `defvaralias`, with WHERE the current buffer when the variable is local if set there (`local-variable-if-set-p`), and the variable untrapped while they run. It walks the live list, which `remove-variable-watcher` splices as `Fdelete` does. Bindings follow `specbind`/`do_one_unbind`: a `let` records the binding before its watchers run; restoring a localized or per-buffer default binding, or binding a per-buffer default, reports `set` with WHERE nil; restoring a global forwarded variable reports `set` then `unlet`, and its `set-default` reports twice; restoring a killed local, and `kill-local-variable` of a forwarded variable, report nothing. A native leaf subr runs in place; any other watcher is funcalled at the write point with collection inhibited until it returns, because the writer's registers and locals are not rooted there (`tests/variable_watchers.rs`). A watcher's signal aborts the write or restore and reaches its handlers once; its `throw` leaves `setq`, `let` and `set` but is refused with a VM2 error when a native primitive (`set-default`, `defvaralias`, `kill-local-variable`) made the write. A code image of a world with watchers is refused
rows.why: **Package-observable**: memory a long-running Lisp watcher allocates is not reclaimed until it returns; a `throw` out of a watcher of a native write signals instead

rows.gnu: `Fframe_parameters` (`src/frame.c:4083`) reports the frame's `buffer-list`/`buried-buffer-list` selection history; `modify-frame-parameters` gives `buffer-list`, `minibuffer`, `parent-frame` and colour parameters their side effects (`store_frame_param`, `update_face_from_frame_parameter`); `internal-show-cursor` hides the cursor at the next redisplay
rows.romacs: VM2 reports GNU's computed entries for a frame without a window system (colours, `font`, `name`, size, `modeline`, menu/tab-bar lines, `visibility`) but nil buffer lists, stores every `modify-frame-parameters` entry as plain data, and records `internal-show-cursor`'s flag (`internal-show-cursor-p` reads it) without the GUI renderer consuming it yet
rows.why: **Package-observable** for code reading a frame's buffer history or relying on colour-parameter side effects; blink-cursor-mode's toggling does not reach the GUI cursor

rows.mechanism: `defvaralias` overwrite warning is printed, not dispatched
rows.gnu: When both variables are bound to different values GNU calls `display-warning` with `(defvaralias losing-value NEW)` and the formatted message (`src/eval.c:686-698`); in batch that prints `Warning (defvaralias): Overwriting value of ‘NEW’ by aliasing to ‘BASE’` to stderr
rows.romacs: VM2 writes that same line to stderr directly; `display-warning` is not called, so `warning-minimum-level`, `warning-suppress-types` and a redefined `display-warning` have no effect, and an interactive session gets no `*Warnings*` buffer
rows.why: **Package-observable** only through warning customisation or a `display-warning` override; the variable state after the call is GNU's

rows.mechanism: Autoload loading: what is still not GNU's
rows.gnu: `Fautoload_do_load` (`src/eval.c:2494`) loads FILE through `load_with_autoload_queue` (`src/eval.c:2465`) when an autoload is called, funcalled, applied (`src/eval.c:2760,3176,3530`), macroexpanded (`src/eval.c:1326`), reached as a keymap (`get_keymap`, `src/keymap.c:218`), asked for its interactive form (`src/data.c:1196`) or run as a command (`src/keyboard.c:10448`). A failed load is undone by `un_autoload` (`src/eval.c:2447`), which re-reads each redefined symbol's previous definition from its `function-history` property (`add_to_function_history`, `src/data.c:933-967`, which keeps one entry per file); `defalias` also honours `defalias-fset-function` and records `load-history`; the "failed to define" error names `(car (car load-history))`, the file as `openp` found it
rows.romacs: Since `vm2/autoload`, calls, `funcall`, `apply`, call requests from primitives (`Step::Call`) and the compiler's macro expansion load the file exactly as GNU (macro expansion now also follows symbol aliases to a macro or macro autoload, as `Fmacroexpand` does at `src/eval.c:1290-1305`; before this lane an alias of a macro compiled as a function call), `autoload-do-load` (1 . 3) matches GNU's argument contract, a failing load reverts function cells and `features` and keeps functions that had no previous definition, nested loads undo only their own level, `require` shares the undo, and match data is saved (`crates/romacs-vm/src/autoload.rs`, tests `tests/autoload_load.rs`, GNU transcript `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/autoload-load/gnu-transcript.txt`; primh row `autoload/0497` now matches and is unpinned). Remaining: (1) VM2 has no `function-history`, so the undo record is the old definition captured at `defalias` time; GNU's re-read differs only if Lisp edits that property mid-load or the same file redefines a symbol it defined on an earlier load; (2) keymap, `interactive-form` and command-loop autoloads are not loaded (VM2 `get_keymap` returns None for an autoload); (3) no `load-history`, so the "Autoloading file %s failed to define function %s" message names the canonicalized path VM2 loaded; (4) `defalias-fset-function` is not honoured; (5) VM2 macroexpands when it compiles the whole top-level form, so a failing macro autoload fails that form's compilation instead of signalling where the call is reached (an enclosing `condition-case` in the same form cannot catch it; see VM2-LAZY4)
rows.why: **Package-observable** for autoloaded keymaps and commands invoked through the command loop before their file is loaded, for code inspecting `function-history`/`load-history`, and through symlinked load paths in the error text. Calling or expanding an autoloaded function or macro behaves as in GNU

rows.mechanism: Symbol property lists: the condition projections, `overriding-plist-environment`, VM-internal command specs, image plists
rows.gnu: GNU stores one plist per symbol object (`u.s.plist`, `src/lisp.h`; marked with the symbol, `src/alloc.c:6673`). `get` first consults `overriding-plist-environment` (`src/fns.c:2653-2663`); `put` is `plist_put` (`src/fns.c:2703-2741`). `symbol-plist` shows every property, including the `error-conditions`/`error-message` that `define-error` puts (live: `((error-conditions (#:c error) error-message "Made") "Made")`), a condition defined only by `setplist` reports its own message (live: `(caught #:c "C!: 1")`), and `(let ((overriding-plist-environment '((foo p 9)))) (get 'foo 'p))` is `9`. Transcripts: `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/plist/gnu-transcript.txt`, `divergence-probe.txt`
rows.romacs: VM2 matches GNU for every other key and case in that transcript, on interned and uninterned symbols alike (`crates/romacs-vm/tests/symbol_plists.rs`): identity-owned plists, any `eq` key, replace in place, append at the end, `plistp`/`circular-list`/`symbolp` signals, nil/t/keyword plists, buffer-local tables kept off the plist. It differs in four ways. (a) `error-conditions` and `error-message` live in VM2's condition registry, not on the plist: `symbol-plist` omits them and `setplist` neither installs nor removes them, so a condition defined only through `setplist` is unknown to `signal` (it is still caught by an `error` handler, as undefined conditions are, but reports `peculiar error: 1` instead of `C!: 1`), and `symbol-plist` after `define-error` is nil instead of GNU's `(error-conditions ... error-message ...)`. (b) `overriding-plist-environment` has its native nil default and dynamic binding; bulk text-property authorization consults it, but general `get` still ignores it (the probe answers nil, GNU 9). (c) A command compiled from `(interactive ...)` carries the VM-internal property `#:interactive` on its plist (GNU keeps the spec in the function object), so `symbol-plist` shows it (live: `(#:interactive (""))` for `(defun f () (interactive) 1)`, GNU nil) and `setplist` removes it. (d) Properties GNU's own C and preloaded Lisp put on symbols are absent until the code that puts them runs in VM2: in batch GNU, `(symbol-plist nil)` is `(event-symbol-element-mask (nil 0) event-symbol-elements (nil) modifier-cache ((0)))` (keyboard.c) and `(symbol-plist t)` adds `cl--class` (cl-preloaded.el); VM2 answers nil for both (primh pins `symbol-plist/0000`, `0001`, `0024`, `0025`, VALUE)
rows.why: **Package-observable** for (a) to (c): code that copies or inspects whole plists (`symbol-plist`, `setplist`, `cl-remprop`-style edits) sees the registry properties missing and a stray `#:interactive`; the byte compiler's `overriding-plist-environment` bindings have no effect. Image-published plists are now private at restoration, preserving aliases through `put` (former item (d), retired by `code_image::image_alias_tests`). Before this row VM2 had no `symbol-plist`/`setplist` at all and refused `get`/`put` on uninterned symbols with `(error "symbol required")`

rows.mechanism: Non-eager regime caches a body's expansion at its first call
rows.gnu: Before `internal-macroexpand-for-load` is fbound, `readevalloop` (`src/lread.c:2183-2188`) evaluates through `eval_sub`, which expands each body form **when it is reached, on every reach, with no cache**: a macro redefined after a function's first call is used by the next call, a macro's expander runs once per reach, and an unreached form is never expanded. Oracle `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/lazy-bodies-oracle.txt`: `(f1 t)` twice expands twice; after redefining the macro `(f1 t)` => `[1]`
rows.romacs: VM2 holds the body unexpanded (traced heap data, `crates/romacs-vm/LAZY-BODIES.md`) and expands **the whole body once, at the first call**, then runs the cached compiled code; only forms whose expansion FAILS are deferred to their reach and re-expanded on every reach until one succeeds. So: an expander runs once, at the first call, not at each reach; a macro redefined after the first call is not seen by that function; a successfully expandable form in a branch that is never taken is still expanded at the first call
rows.why: **Package-observable** only through macro side effects or macro redefinition between calls of a function defined before macroexp.el is loaded, i.e. during the bootstrap chain (subr.el and anything else loaded before `emacs-lisp/macroexp`). Files loaded after macroexp.el are in GNU's eager regime, where VM2 already matches GNU's timing. Compiling per form on every reach would mean interpreting

rows.mechanism: The eager regime is VM2's compiler, not `internal-macroexpand-for-load`
rows.gnu: Once `internal-macroexpand-for-load` is fbound, GNU **calls** it on every top-level form (`readevalloop_eager_expand_eval`), so macroexp.el's Lisp expander, its `macroexp--pending-eager-loads` `skip` protocol and cycle detection decide expansion, and a failure is the error `Eager macro-expansion failure: ERR`. `eval` never expands eagerly
rows.romacs: VM2 only tests `fboundp internal-macroexpand-for-load` to choose the regime (once per `load`, like GNU); in the eager regime its own compiler expands the whole form, so the function is never called, `macroexp--pending-eager-loads` is not consulted, and a failure reports VM2's own text (the macro's condition text, or a native-expander message), not `Eager macro-expansion failure: ...`. `eval` follows the regime of the load that is running (eager outside any non-eager load), where GNU's `eval` is always non-eager
rows.why: **Package-observable:** a redefinition of `internal-macroexpand-for-load` does not change expansion; loadup's pcase `'(skip)` dance does not make pcase.el lazy; error text of an eager failure differs; an `eval`'d definition whose body fails to expand fails at the `eval` in eager context where GNU defers it to the call

rows.gnu: `Finterpreted_function_p` (`src/data.c:541`) is t iff the object is a closure whose code slot is a cons: any function from `.el` source (eagerly expanded or not), never a subr or byte-code. In a dumped GNU the preloaded functions are byte-compiled, so `(interpreted-function-p (symbol-function 'add-hook))` => nil there and t only in `bootstrap-emacs`
rows.romacs: VM2 has no byte-code: every closure it builds from Lisp source answers t, every primitive nil (oracle rows: `car` nil, `nil` nil, `(lambda (x) x)` t, arity `(1 . 1)`). It does NOT report whether a body is still unexpanded, and neither does GNU's
rows.why: **Package-observable** for preloaded (subr.el, files.el, ...) functions, which answer t where a dumped GNU answers nil; `loadup.el:181` therefore takes its bootstrap-emacs branch and requires gv. `compiled-function-p`/`byte-code-function-p` are not implemented

rows.gnu: In the non-eager regime GNU signals whatever the reached form signals: an unknown head such as a not-yet-loaded `setf` is `(void-function setf)` (gv.el not loaded) or gv's own error, an invalid lambda list is `(invalid-function ...)` at the call, and the interpreted closure keeps only the variables it captures once cconv is loaded
rows.romacs: A deferred form whose failure came from a Lisp macro re-signals that macro's structured condition (matches GNU, test `reach_time_expansion_keeps_a_non_error_condition_structured`); a failure from VM2's **native** expanders (native `setf` places, malformed special forms) signals `(error "MESSAGE")` with VM2's text. A malformed lambda list is still rejected when the closure is created, not when it is called. A lazily held closure captures every visible lexical binding until its first call
rows.why: **Package-observable:** `condition-case` on a reached native-`setf` failure sees `error`, not `void-function`; a defun with an invalid argument list fails at definition. Capturing the whole environment only retains memory

rows.mechanism: `make-variable-buffer-local` of a void variable leaves its default void
rows.gnu: `Fmake_variable_buffer_local` (`src/data.c:2178`, line 2214) sets a void variable's default value to nil before making it automatically buffer-local, so `(progn (make-variable-buffer-local 'v) (default-boundp 'v))` is t
rows.romacs: VM2's `make-variable-buffer-local` installs the local table without touching the default, so the default stays void: `default-boundp` (which itself matches GNU on every other harness row) answers nil, and `default-value`/reading the variable in a buffer without a local signal `void-variable`. The one pinned `default-boundp` harness row, `default-boundp/0034`, is exactly this
rows.why: **Package-observable** for code that makes a never-set variable automatically buffer-local and then reads its default; a `defvar` with a value first (the usual pattern) behaves as in GNU

rows.mechanism: Only the built-in (C) variables the bootstrap reaches exist, with C-time values
rows.gnu: GNU defines 948 variables in C (618 `DEFVAR_LISP`, 196 `DEFVAR_BOOL`, 74 `DEFVAR_INT`, 60 `DEFVAR_PER_BUFFER`); each symbol is `SYMBOL_FORWARDED` to C storage from startup, and a dumped GNU then runs `loadup.el`'s Lisp, which fills several of them (`minibuffer-local-map` gains its bindings, `window-persistent-parameters` gains `(context . writable)`, `load-file-rep-suffixes` gains `".gz"` from jka-cmpr-hook.el)
rows.romacs: VM2 forwards the subset declared in `crates/romacs-vm/src/forwarded.rs`, with each entry citing its DEFVAR and the census or chain need that pulled it in, with GNU's forwarding semantics for `symbol-value`, `set`/`setq`, `let` (including unwinding on a signal), `default-value`, `set-default`, `makunbound` (`Built-in variable may not be unbound`), bool coercion, int `integerp` checks and per-buffer auto-local behaviour; GNU 32.0.50 transcripts in `crates/romacs-vm/evidence/c-variables/`. Values are the C initial values, not the dumped image's: `minibuffer-local-map` is `(keymap)`, `window-persistent-parameters` is `((clone-of . t))`, `load-file-rep-suffixes` is `("")`, so `(get-load-suffixes)` is `(".so" ".elc" ".el")` where `emacs -Q` gives `(".so" ".elc" ".elc.gz" ".el" ".el.gz")` (pinned rows `get-load-suffixes/0000`, `/0002`). Other GNU built-ins are ordinary symbols: void until Lisp sets them, not special unless `defvar`ed, and any value is accepted
rows.why: **Package-observable:** reading an undefined built-in signals `void-variable`; a `let` of one binds lexically under `lexical-binding`; VM2 does not look for compressed `.el.gz` files. Grows as the census pulls variables in, never speculatively (R216)

rows.gnu: `make-local-variable` / `make-variable-buffer-local` of a `DEFVAR_LISP`/`BOOL`/`INT` variable turns it into `SYMBOL_LOCALIZED` over the forwarding (`src/data.c:2178-2300`, a `blv` whose `fwd` is the C storage): `(with-temp-buffer (make-local-variable 'undo-limit) (setq undo-limit 5) (list undo-limit (default-value 'undo-limit)))` => `(5 160000)`
rows.romacs: VM2 supports localized global Boolean variables through the existing traced local-binding tables and retained native default storage. Current/local writes coerce non-nil values to t; dynamic cleanup, buffer changes and recreated local bindings retain their Boolean values. Localized Boolean defaults and saved defaults accept only nil or t; noncanonical writes, or promotion while a saved default is noncanonical, signal an explicit VM2 error. GNU can retain a raw default until a buffer transition synchronizes its C storage, which VM2 does not model. Object and integer globals still signal `VM2 cannot make built-in variable buffer-local`; `DEFVAR_PER_BUFFER` variables retain their existing behavior. Code images retain the existing refusal of localized state
rows.why: **Package-observable** for object/integer localization and noncanonical localized Boolean defaults. Ordinary Boolean localization used by GNU help and JSON formatting is supported

rows.mechanism: Invalid representation suffix signals instead of crashing
rows.gnu: GNU 32.0.50 `Fget_load_suffixes` (`src/lread.c:961`) exits 139 (SIGSEGV) for `(progn (setq load-file-rep-suffixes (list 42)) (get-load-suffixes))`; its concatenation does not check the element type
rows.romacs: VM2's checked `concat` signals `(wrong-type-argument sequencep 42)` instead. Regression `get_load_suffixes_rejects_gnu_crashing_rep_suffix` rejects a mutant that silently returns nil
rows.why: **Intentional safety divergence:** malformed input is catchable with `condition-case`, never a process crash

rows.mechanism: Empty strings are not one shared object
rows.gnu: GNU has exactly two empty strings, `empty_unibyte_string` and `empty_multibyte_string` (`src/alloc.c:1557-1562`), and every length-0 string allocation returns one of them (`src/alloc.c:2330,2359`), including `copy-sequence` of `""` and a string emptied by `delete` (`src/fns.c:2137`): `(eq (copy-sequence "") (copy-sequence ""))` is t
rows.romacs: VM2 allocates a fresh empty string each time, so that witness is nil (true before `delete` existed). `delete` itself follows GNU exactly: it returns SEQ when nothing matched and a new string of SEQ's kind otherwise; only the identity of an emptied result differs. The one pinned `delete` harness row, `delete/0680` (`(eq r a0)` for two `(copy-sequence "")`), is exactly this
rows.why: **Package-observable** only through `eq` (or `memq`/`assq`) between separately produced empty strings; `equal`, `string=`, length and multibyteness agree. A canonical empty string belongs in the allocator, not in each primitive

rows.gnu: GNU's C maintains both while it loads: `load` specbinds `current-load-list` to `(FILE)` (`loadhist_initialize`, `src/lread.c:1031-1035`), `build_load_history` (`src/lread.c:2054-2114`) moves it into `load-history`, and `load` then calls `do-after-load-evaluation` (`src/lread.c:1539-1540`); `LOADHIST_ATTACH` (`src/lisp.h:4735-4739`) conses onto `current-load-list` from `defvar` (`src/eval.c:913`), `defalias` (`src/data.c:979`), `defvaralias` (`src/eval.c:721`), `provide` and `require` (`src/fns.c:3759`, `src/fns.c:3824`). Harness rows `defvar/036` and `defvar/038`: after `(defvar current-load-list 99)` GNU's `current-load-list` is a new cons, so `(eq current-load-list old)` is nil
rows.romacs: Romacs binds `current-load-list` to `(FILE)` for each load, with FILE the name the file was found by (expanded, not resolved through symlinks, as GNU's `hist_file_name`), replaces the file's `load-history` entry with it when the load completes, then calls `do-after-load-evaluation`; `provide` funcalls its `after-load-alist` entry (`tests/real_ert_load.rs`). Variable declarations can attach entries, but `defalias`, `defvar`, `provide` and `require` do not, so an entry usually holds only FILE. Backtraces therefore lack source-file cross-references from load history. `eval-buffer` and `eval-region` remain unsupported, so `eval-buffer-list` stays nil. The two rows above remain pinned VALUE
rows.why: **Package-observable** for code that inspects `current-load-list` or what `load-history` records about definitions (`symbol-file`, `unload-feature`, `find-function` by load history)

rows.mechanism: Loader failures outside Lisp runtime execution remain textual
rows.gnu: GNU runtime signals escaping `load`, `require` and `autoload-do-load` retain their condition and data
rows.romacs: Lisp runtime loading now carries the original condition, data object and selected handler across loader reentry before cleanup. Live GNU comparisons cover ordinary errors, primitive type errors, cyclic aliases, require and autoload signals; returning-handler tests also retain the same error object through GC and unwind. The Rust embedder `load_file` interface still returns textual errors, and source-read/compile failures without a runtime escape use that interface. Compile-time macro-autoload placement remains VM2-LAZY4
rows.why: **Package-observable** for source-read/compile failures; ordinary runtime signals retain their payload

rows.mechanism: Re-entrant `load` of a file already being loaded
rows.gnu: `Fload` refuses a file only when it is already being loaded more than three times (`src/lread.c:1309-1314`, "Recursive load"); `Frequire` refuses a feature only when it is already being required more than three times (`src/fns.c`, "Recursive `require' for feature `%s'"). `provide` takes effect when evaluated, so a file that provides before requiring its partner (calendar.el:163 then :164) satisfies the partner's `require` mid-load; a file whose partner requires it BEFORE it provides is loaded again, nested, and that is fine in GNU. Measured (`crates/romacs-vm/evidence/autoload-load/cyclic-require.txt`): loading calendar, org, org-agenda, gnus and vc-git from source makes 892 requires with 7 re-entrant ones, 6 already satisfied by an early `provide` and ONE genuine nested reload, `gnus-sum.el` required again from `gnus-group.el`
rows.romacs: `provide` is immediate in VM2 too, so every early-provide cycle (calendar/cal-menu, cl-lib/cl-macs, cl-lib/cl-seq) behaves as in GNU, and the late-provide cycle errors as GNU does (condition `error`, VM2's text). But VM2's loader refuses ANY re-entrant load of a file still being loaded ("recursive source load"), so a file that loads itself, and the gnus-sum/gnus-group shape, fail where GNU succeeds (fixture: GNU `(gs 2 (gg gs))`, VM2 `(error)`)
rows.why: **Package-observable** for Gnus (`gnus-sum`) and any file that re-enters its own load. Org and calendar do not need it. Not changed by vm2/autoload; belongs to the loader

rows.mechanism: A symbol with an empty name prints as nothing
rows.gnu: `print_object`, Lisp_Symbol arm (`src/print.c:2496-2500`): with `print-gensym` nil (or for an interned symbol) a zero-byte name prints `##`, so `(prin1-to-string (intern ""))` and `(prin1-to-string (make-symbol ""))` are both `"##"`
rows.romacs: VM2's printer emits the empty name verbatim, so both are `""` (and `(list (intern "") (make-symbol ""))` prints `( )`); true before `keywordp` existed (the 23deaa2a binary gives the same rows). The symbols themselves agree: `symbol-name`, `eq` and `keywordp` (nil for both, harness rows `keywordp/0026`, `/0027`). The two pinned `keywordp` harness rows, `keywordp/0071` and `/0079`, are the printer family of these two values and call no `keywordp`
rows.why: **Package-observable** only when printing the empty-named symbol (`prin1`, `format "%S"`), whose GNU output `##` reads back as that symbol and VM2's empty output does not. Belongs in the printer, not in any primitive

rows.gnu: GNU's initial obarray is a bucket-ordered table, counts every symbol, resets an invalid current `obarray` to the initial table before signalling, and permits removing its nil/t symbols.
rows.romacs: VM2's initial object lazily projects the existing compiler name table. `mapatoms` uses stable slot order (custom tables use GNU bucket order), its printed count includes only subsequent explicit insertions, nil/t remain canonical, and invalid current bindings are rejected without GNU's reset. Live witnesses `evidence/obarray-substrate/divergence-probes.json`: `invalid-current-reset` is GNU t / VM2 nil; filtered initial order differs. Removing compiler-known names also retains existing name-keyed compiler/variable metadata.
rows.why: **Package-observable default-table limitations**, not full initial-obarray parity. Custom obarray lookup, identity, removal, iteration and GC are independently tested.

rows.gnu: GNU accepts arbitrary Emacs strings, comparing both exact bytes and character count.
rows.romacs: Custom obarrays retain exact input-name objects and compare bytes/characters, but construction still requires a Unicode-decodable name for the existing symbol-slot metadata. `(intern (unibyte-string 255) (obarray-make))` signals `not-unicode-string`; GNU returns a symbol. The initial name table also conflates equal UTF-8 bytes with differing character counts. Live transcript: `evidence/obarray-substrate/divergence-probes.json`, `raw-name`. Existing name-based constant checks described in VM2-BOOT4 can also affect custom symbols.
rows.why: **Package-observable symbol-substrate boundary**; no byte coercion or invented replacement symbol is returned.

rows.mechanism: Reader and image integration of obarrays
rows.gnu: GNU's reader interns into the current `obarray`, and its dumped runtime retains the initial obarray.
rows.romacs: VM2's existing reader still interns source names into the compiler name table: `(let ((obarray (obarray-make))) (eq (car (read-from-string "obarray-gap-x")) (intern "obarray-gap-x" obarray)))` is GNU t / VM2 nil (live transcript in `evidence/obarray-substrate/divergence-probes.json`). First-class obarrays are mutable heap objects, so the existing immutable-string/cons-only code-image publisher refuses them; this slice does not add an image codec or alter bootstrap/loadup. Constructing an evaluated call whose head is a custom symbol also reaches the existing generated-symbol compiler restriction (`generated-call-head` in the same transcript: GNU 1, VM2 `symbol required`); ordinary `(funcall SYMBOL)` does not need that source conversion.
rows.why: **Package-observable integration boundaries** outside the custom-collection API. Completion can consume an explicitly supplied obarray through the leaf cursor without relying on reader redirection.

rows.mechanism: General formatting and initial locale capability
rows.gnu: `format-message` has all `format` conversions and text-property/identity behavior; the initial internal quoting flag follows the process locale.
rows.romacs: Quote selection, template-only substitution, explicit capability bindings, display-table fallback and byte8 promotion are implemented. The shared formatter supports field numbers, flags, width and precision for `%s`, `%S`, `%c`, `%d`, `%i`, `%b`, `%B`, `%o`, `%x`, `%X`, `%e`, `%f`, `%g` and `%%`, including bignum integers and float rounding. Width, precision and field-number components are capped at 2^20. Text-property propagation and GNU string-identity behavior remain unsupported. Initial capability is the VM UTF-8 default (`t`), without host non-UTF-8 locale detection, and the capability binding is not boolean-normalized.
rows.why: `tests/format_numeric.rs` compares the formatting domain with pinned GNU; the separate 64-case quoting corpus does not establish text-property, identity or host-locale parity.

rows.gnu: GNU `lread.c:openp` checks the suffixed candidate for a `file-exists-p` handler, then uses `file-readable-p` when selected; expansion can also dispatch `expand-file-name`. `fileio.c:find-file-name-handler` selects the latest-starting matching regexp (first on ties), respects handler `operations` and operation-specific inhibition, ignores case-fold-search, and preserves match data.
rows.romacs: VM2 now permits local lookup with unrelated, operation-filtered or inhibited handlers. It implements native handler selection but still explicitly refuses a selected non-nil handler with `VM2 locate-file-internal matching file name handler is unsupported`; it also retains the non-nil predicate refusal. This conservative refusal includes an existing `file-exists-p` handler even if GNU's subsequent `file-readable-p` lookup would use the local filesystem. Other file I/O primitives retain their existing blanket handler refusal (VM2-FILEIO1). GNU's recursive relative-directory expansion, non-string-root `/` fallback and `/:` quoting prefix are not reproduced by this pre-existing path expander; handlers that require those transformations remain unsupported.
rows.why: No Lisp handler dispatch or general handler stack is implemented. Regression coverage: `tests/locate_file_handlers.rs`; oracle pin `45b0f7699df36b3849edc3bdef37d4cb9e75b9ea`, GNU 32.0.50.

rows.section: Observable by a package: circular completion tables
rows.gnu: GNU traverses until an exact test match, a decisive common prefix, or user quit; some circular inputs never finish.
rows.romacs: Decisive early results are preserved. Traversal that would revisit a detected cycle signals `circular-list`.
rows.why: Bounded native traversal with callback state traced across GC. `tests/completion.rs` covers both early-result cases.

rows.section: Observable by a package: circular completion tables
rows.mechanism: Completion case folding and string comparison
rows.gnu: GNU uses its current case tables, with nil entries meaning identity.
rows.romacs: Original native tables retain Unicode fallback for nil entries above ASCII before GNU enrichment. Explicit non-nil entries override it; ASCII and replacement-table nil entries mean identity.
rows.why: Preserve the native Unicode startup policy while respecting explicit ASCII edits and replacement tables. Range-crossing and replacement-table tests cover the boundary.

rows.mechanism: Closure metadata and GNU generic dispatch
rows.gnu: GNU OClosure inspects closure documentation and captured environment slots.
rows.romacs: Ordinary closures retain a private traced documentation value. The explicit `oclosure--fix-type` marker emitted by GNU's macro retains named capture cells and exposes the supported interpreter metadata. `romacs-cl-generic` loads the owned `romacs-oclosure` type-query bridge before unchanged GNU `cl-generic`.
rows.why: Compatibility callers must load the named entry after GNU core prerequisites; this is not an automatic GUI startup addition. Ordinary closure array access remains rejected. Explicit OClosure capture retention may include bindings GNU optimizes away. Existing code-image restrictions on mutable captured cells remain. Code images use VM2CODE8 to serialize private documentation. `tests/oclosure.rs` covers accessors, copying, inheritance, identity, GC, dispatch, replacement and method combination.

rows.mechanism: Explicit batch adapter and compiled backtrace metadata
rows.gnu: ERT isolates each test with a temporary buffer and a window excursion; GNU backtraces can describe interpreter/source frames and lexical locals.
rows.romacs: The named `romacs-batch` adapter retains the temporary buffer, assertions, error handling, cleanup, expectedness and GNU batch runner, and replaces the precautionary window excursion. Condition objects use `prin1` plus a newline instead of editor indentation; their data and expectedness are unchanged. Automatic window-layout restoration and GUI fixtures are unsupported. Backtraces report real compiled calls, original evaluated argument snapshots and dynamic locals; lexical/source locals, pre-argument named-autoload frames and debugger mutation are unavailable. GNU apply optimizations can produce different frame/argument shapes. Ordinary closures print opaquely through an owned `cl-print-object` method.
rows.why: Keep the batch regime explicit and preserve private closure representation.

rows.mechanism: Bulk text-property edits and forward boundary queries
rows.gnu: GNU supports arbitrary property keys, modification callbacks, byte buffers and raw interval traversal with `next-property-change` LIMIT t.
rows.romacs: Bulk edits support interned symbol keys, mutable strings and annotated text buffers, with atomic validation, read-only checks and a changed-result flag. Unibyte buffers are edited too, and change hooks run as VM2-EDIT-HOOKS1 describes. Other key types and immutable image-string writes refuse explicitly. The two forward queries support strings and annotated text buffers; unibyte-buffer queries and raw interval LIMIT t refuse explicitly. Effective property queries retain the existing general property-resolution limits.
rows.why: Reuse the native property runs and overlay precedence for the ERT printer's actual calls.

rows.section: Observable by a user: workspace file coding
rows.mechanism: File coding in the default workspace (no loadup)
rows.gnu: GNU's image has all of mule-conf.el and the language environments; `set-locale-environment` for a UTF-8 locale on GNU/Linux puts `utf-8` first in `coding-system-priority-list` and makes the default `buffer-file-coding-system` and `default-file-name-coding-system` `utf-8-unix`. Visiting also consults `set-auto-coding-function` (`set-auto-coding`: `auto-coding-alist`, `auto-coding-regexp-alist`, `coding:` cookies, `auto-coding-functions`) and `file-coding-system-alist`; saving consults `select-safe-coding-system-function` (`select-safe-coding-system`, which asks through `select-safe-coding-system-interactively` when no default coding system encodes the text, and warns and asks before writing under a cookie that names an unknown coding system), and `basic-save-buffer-2` keeps `last-coding-system-used` as `buffer-file-coding-system`.
rows.romacs: Startup (`initialize_coding`, `crates/romacs-vm-gui/src/startup.rs`) evaluates verbatim from the pinned mirror mule.el's `define-coding-system`, `coding-system-type`, `buffer-file-coding-system-explicit`, `after-insert-file-set-coding` and `find-new-buffer-file-coding-system`, and mule-conf.el's fundamental aliases, `prefer-utf-8`, `raw-text`, `no-conversion-multibyte`, `iso-latin-1` (`iso-8859-1`, `latin-1`), the `utf-8`, `utf-8-with-signature`, `utf-8-auto` and `utf-8-emacs` definitions with their aliases, and the `latin-extra-code-table` entries. It also evaluates mule.el's auto-coding machinery (`auto-coding-alist`, `auto-coding-regexp-alist`, `auto-coding-functions` with `sgml-xml-auto-coding-function` and `sgml-html-meta-auto-coding-function`, `find-auto-coding`, `set-auto-coding`, `coding-system-get`, `coding-system-category`, `coding-system-equal`) and its `(setq set-auto-coding-function ...)`, and mule-cmds.el's `select-safe-coding-system` with `find-coding-systems-region`, `sort-coding-systems`, `coding-system-change-eol-conversion`, `coding-system-change-text-conversion`, `get-language-info` (`language-info-alist` nil, `current-language-environment` "English") and its `(setq select-safe-coding-system-function ...)`, together with the helpers they call from files.el (`set-auto-mode-1`, `inhibit-local-variables-p`, `file-name-sans-versions`, `find-file-literally`), subr.el (`caar`, `ignore-errors`, `string-match-p`, `ensure-list`), byte-run.el (`defsubst` and its `eval-and-compile`, `function-put`, `byte-run--set-speed`) and mule-util.el (`with-coding-priority`). `rlisp/romacs-coding.el` then sets GNU's UTF-8-locale result restricted to those systems: priority `utf-8 iso-latin-1 raw-text utf-8-auto utf-8-with-signature undecided` and the `utf-8-unix` defaults; it assumes a UTF-8 locale. Its one adaptation replaces the question: the workspace cannot show GNU's *Warning* explanation (temp-buffer display, help buttons, fill), so `select-safe-coding-system-interactively` signals `romacs-unsafe-coding` with the unsafe defaults and the safe systems GNU would offer; `write-region` has not opened the file, which keeps its bytes, and the buffer stays modified. The workspace save (`romacs-gui-write-visited-buffer`, `rlisp/romacs-startup.el`) keeps `last-coding-system-used` as GNU's `basic-save-buffer-1` and `-2` do. No other coding system is defined (ISO-2022, UTF-16, CJK, other ISO-8859 sets), and `file-coding-system-alist` stays nil.
rows.why: UTF-8 (LF and CRLF), ASCII and Latin-1 files (with or without a cookie, agreeing with the bytes or not) and a UTF-8 file with a BOM visit, edit and save as pinned GNU does: decoded text, `last-coding-system-used`, `buffer-file-coding-system` and bytes on disk, including λ typed into a Latin-1 file (saved as UTF-8) and text typed before a BOM (kept after the signature) (`crates/romacs-vm-gui/src/command.rs` `coding_journey_visits_edits_and_saves_as_pinned_gnu`); where pinned GNU asks (λ under a `coding: latin-1` cookie) C-x C-s signals `romacs-unsafe-coding` with GNU's unsafe defaults and its safe systems that the workspace defines, before writing (`coding_save_refuses_where_pinned_gnu_would_ask`). **User-observable**: (1) where GNU asks which coding system to save with, the workspace refuses the save; (2) a cookie or signature naming a coding system the workspace does not define (e.g. `coding: euc-jp`, a UTF-16 BOM) is ignored by the visit, which detection decides, and saving then signals `void-function display-warning` before writing where GNU warns and asks `Really proceed with writing?` (warnings.el is absent); (3) `detect-coding-region` is not implemented, so GNU's `sgml-xml-auto-coding-function` fails inside its `ignore-errors` for an XML declaration without `encoding=`, and detection decides (`undecided-unix` for ASCII XML where GNU names `utf-8-unix`); (4) bytes only an undefined coding detects (C1 bytes outside `latin-extra-code-table`, which GNU decodes as `japanese-shift-jis`; UTF-16; ISO-2022) refuse the visit (`raw bytes into a multibyte buffer` or a detector refusal), leaving the file untouched.
